applicability: The subject vehicle enters an intersection (its footprint comes to overlap the junction region at the observation) and, at that entry observation, a traffic-control signal governs that intersection, is installed with its vehicular faces uncovered, and is inoperative.
obligation: Before that entry the subject must have come to a complete halt at the place the words name, in their order. The event is the subject's entry into that intersection; the target is the approach carrier the subject occupies whose entrance end is that intersection. The place is the stop line recorded as marking that carrier; where the carrier's stop lines are observed and none marks it, the crosswalk recorded as marking that carrier; where neither is marked, the point on that carrier nearest the intersection at which the sight along the crossing way, in the lesser of its two directions, is at least p.intersecting_way_view_distance. A halt counts at the place when the subject's speed is at or below p.standstill_speed_tolerance while the distance between its body and the mark is at most p.stop_point_tolerance and it has not yet passed the mark, the side being read by the sign of prim.region_offset_along along the carrier's designated direction; a halt whose footprint already overlaps the intersection is not at the place. The search for the halt runs back from the entry observation and ends at the start of that approach -- the last observation before the entry at which the subject, on a carrier the mark marks, was off the mark, short of it and farther from it than p.stop_point_tolerance -- or at the previous entry of the same subject into the same intersection, and at nothing else: not at another junction, not at the first observation of the recording, not at a distance travelled. Where the search finds the halt the duty is met; where it reaches either end without it the duty is violated; where it reaches neither end, because the history the bound needs begins before the recording or because the carrier's association with the mark or the carrier's direction is not observed, the duty is unknown. Where the stop line's entrances are observed and exclude the subject's carrier, the place is read from the next words in order and the duty is not unknown on that ground.

narrowings.why: 'shall proceed as if a stop sign had been erected at each entrance to the intersection' is read through the conduct the same sentence and the next one prescribe -- the halt at the place and, in the second node, the cautious proceeding with its yielding -- and not through a stop-sign device: no stop sign is present in the scene, and reading one in would make the rule turn on a device the trace does not show.

'a clearly marked stop line' is read as the stop line the scene represents: the line's presence is the evidence of its clear marking, and the paint's clarity or wear is not modelled. The reading relaxes neither which place governs nor the halt and its timing.

'the through highway' is read as the highway the subject's approach crosses at that intersection: DEF-NRS-484A-275 makes a through highway one at whose entrances traffic is required by law to yield in obedience to a stop sign, a yield sign or other device, which is a legal designation no feature of a scene with an inoperative signal displays; the words' purpose here is the view of the traffic the subject must give way to, and that traffic approaches on the crossing way.

'has a view of approaching traffic' is read as the sight along the crossing way reaching at least p.intersecting_way_view_distance in the lesser of its two directions, and not as the driver's actual perception, which no trace carries.

'the driver of the vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: who or what is at the controls is not observable, a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven, and the duty binds that vehicle's conduct.

'the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic' is written as: at rest on the approach carrier, its footprint not yet over the junction, with the sight along the crossing way at least p.intersecting_way_view_distance. No region of a scene marks that point, and a trace carries sampled positions only, so the place is not stated as the minimum over the points of the carrier at which the view holds; every point of the carrier, short of the junction, from which the way is visible that far counts as the place.

'the through highway' on which the traffic approaches is written as a highway region the junction lies on (st.on_way) that the subject's carrier does not lie on — the way the approach crosses there. Where the source records several such ways, the view along any one of them satisfies the place; a way the source does not record leaves no view, so the place is not reached.

Where the place is the view point, the start of the approach that ends the search back has no mark to be measured from: it is written as the stretch of the carrier, short of the junction, at which the sight along the crossing way does not yet reach p.intersecting_way_view_distance — the same relation to the place that the mark's upstream zone has to a mark.

The end of the search at 'the previous entry of the same subject into the same intersection' is written as the subject's own presence in that junction (rel.occupies), read at an observation before the judged entry: a formula read at the judged entry cannot tell that entry from an earlier one, and the two bounds decide this duty alike, because no halt at the place can be found while the subject's footprint overlaps the junction. The duty is judged at the observation before the entry for the same reason.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car approaches a four-way junction whose signal heads are installed, uncovered and dark with no valid indication. A stop line is recorded as marking the lane the car occupies, the lane's entrance end is that junction, and the car crosses the line and enters the junction without its speed ever falling to the standstill tolerance anywhere on the approach from the line's upstream zone onward. No other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same junction and the same inoperative signal. The car halts with its speed at zero while its body is within the stop-point tolerance of the stop line marking its lane and short of the line, then moves off and enters the junction. The scene contains no other road user, and the verdict is still decided.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The same junction, but the signal governing it shows a steady circular red and is not inoperative. The car enters the junction without halting: the trigger does not hold, so the rule is not engaged.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The car enters the junction without halting, the signal is installed and uncovered, but the source does not report whether the head is showing a valid indication, so whether it was inoperative at the entry is unknown and the rule reports unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A junction with the same inoperative signal where the lane's stop lines and crosswalks are observed and none marks the car's lane. The car halts, with its speed at zero, on its lane at the point nearest the junction at which the sight along the crossing way reaches the view distance, then enters: the third place in the words' order governs and the duty is met.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The same junction and inoperative signal, with no stop line but a marked crosswalk recorded as marking the car's lane. The car slows to a crawl above the standstill tolerance before the crosswalk and rolls into the junction: the second place in the words' order governs and no halt is found on the approach.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: The recording begins with the car already between the stop line and the junction, inside the line's stopping zone, and the car then enters the junction while the signal is inoperative. No halt is recorded, and the recording contains neither the start of the approach upstream of the line nor a previous entry of the car into that junction, so no recorded act and no visible end of the search decides the verdict.
scenarios.boundary: the stretch of the approach upstream of the stop line's stopping zone, at which the car entered that zone, lies before the first observation of the recording

param_proposals.name: p.standstill_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Standstill convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed reading is read as the complete cessation from movement DEF-NRS-484A-255 requires, set at the noise floor of a speed channel at rest.
param_proposals.source: Instrumentation practice for speed channels in scene-graph traces, whose residual at rest stays below a tenth of a metre per second.

param_proposals.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Stop-point convention of the approach reading: the bound within which a halt counts as at the place the words name -- the stop line, the crosswalk or the view point -- covering the width of the marking and the position error of the body outline.
param_proposals.source: Marking-geometry and localisation practice: a transverse line about half a metre wide plus the position error of a body outline.

param_proposals.name: p.intersecting_way_view_distance
param_proposals.convention: Intersection sight-distance convention: the length of the intersecting way that must be visible in each direction from the stopping point for approaching traffic to be seen before the crossing is begun.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book intersection sight-distance tables for a crossing manoeuvre at urban approach speeds.

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a steady yellow signal alone:
Vehicular traffic facing the signal
is thereby warned that the related green movement is being terminated or that a steady red indication will be exhibited immediately thereafter,
and such vehicular traffic must not enter the intersection
when the red signal is exhibited.

elements.justification: 'the signal is a steady yellow signal alone' is dev.traffic_signal, 'a signal head', read in its state circular_yellow: the enumeration lists circular_yellow for a steady yellow face, and since 'several states may be displayed at once', 'alone' is read as that state being displayed and no other state of the head being displayed at the observation. The atom is a device and not a sign, and no sign atom is claimed; the head read is the one governing the subject's approach, which the subject span binds.

'traffic' is the term DEF-NRS-484A-285 defines, 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel', admitted as the aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and claimed as one atom. The law's own word 'vehicular' qualifies it and limits which of its members the duty reads: of the classes the definition includes -- pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances -- the duty reads the vehicles, leaving out pedestrians and ridden or herded animals, so the admitted aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle is claimed beside it as the second class element, each as one atom and neither expanded into the classes it covers. 'facing the signal' is read as the ontology directs for an approach: the road user occupies (rel.occupies) a carrier of kind st.travel_region whose entrance end is the intersection (st.lane_enters, st.intersection) and which the head governs, dev.governs being 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', with dev.traffic_signal the head itself. dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position, and the facing is not read from the subject's heading: the ontology fixes which approach a road user is on by the carrier it occupies and that carrier's entrance, never by its velocity or heading.

'must not enter the intersection' is the event drv.motion.region_entry denotes, 'the road user's footprint comes to overlap a structure region at the observation ... the event of that coming to overlap', read on the junction region of kind st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges') that the subject's carrier enters, with rel.occupies the anchor to the subject's own footprint and the kind-ranging relation the region quantifier needs. The concept is the entry and not the lying inside: a road user already within the junction when the red is exhibited makes no entry, which is what the words forbid. st.intersection is not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line.

'when the red signal is exhibited' is dev.traffic_signal in its state circular_red, the enumeration's value for a steady red face, read on the same head that governs the subject's carrier (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'), so that a red face governing another approach of the junction does not forbid this entry. The condition is read at the observation of the entry the obligation judges, since the words tie the exhibition to the moment of entering.

residues.why: 'is thereby warned that the related green movement is being terminated or that a steady red indication will be exhibited immediately thereafter' adds no observable condition to the prohibition: it states what the yellow face tells the driver, and the duty that follows is the same whether or not the green movement is in fact being terminated or the red in fact follows immediately. What a driver was warned of is a state of mind no trace carries, and reading the clause as a condition would make the rule apply only where the signal's programme is known, which is narrower than the words.

applicability: The subject is a road user of the traffic aggregate that is also a vehicle, occupying a carrier whose entrance end is an intersection and which a traffic-signal head governs, and that head displayed a steady circular yellow and no other state at the judged observation or at an earlier observation while the subject was on that carrier.
obligation: The subject must not enter that intersection -- its footprint must not come to overlap the junction region -- at an observation at which the head governing its carrier exhibits a steady circular red.

narrowings.why: The words join a trigger stated of the yellow face to a prohibition conditioned on the red face, which the head cannot display as its only state at one and the same observation. The prohibition is therefore read over the approach: the duty arises for a road user that faced the steady yellow alone on that carrier, and it forbids an entry made at an observation at which the governing head exhibits the red. A reading that required both faces at one observation would make the prohibition empty.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car occupies a lane that enters a signalised junction, and the head governing that lane shows a steady circular yellow alone. Two seconds later the head shows circular red, and at that observation the car's footprint comes to overlap the junction region for the first time.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same lane and head. The car faces the steady yellow, brakes and comes to rest short of the junction, its footprint never overlapping the junction region while the head shows red; no other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The head governing the car's lane shows a steady circular green throughout and never a steady yellow alone: the trigger never holds and the rule is not engaged, even though the car enters the junction.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The car faces the steady yellow and later enters the junction, but at the entry observation the source reports no state for the head governing its lane, so whether the red was exhibited is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The car faces the steady yellow and crosses into the junction while the head still shows the yellow, the red appearing only after its whole body is inside: the entry was not made at an observation at which the red was exhibited.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian on a crosswalk at the same junction faces the same head after it has shown steady yellow alone and steps into the junction region while the red is exhibited: the subject is not of the vehicle aggregate, so the duty this rule states does not bind it.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
within an intersection
intending to turn to the left
shall yield the right-of-way to any vehicle approaching from the opposite direction which is within the intersection
or so close thereto as to constitute an immediate hazard,

but such driver, having so yielded and having given a signal when and as required, may make such left turn and the drivers of all other vehicles approaching the intersection from the opposite direction shall yield the right-of-way to the vehicle making the left turn.

elements.justification: 'The driver of a vehicle' binds the subject: DEF-NRS-484A-080 makes the driver the person who drives or is in actual physical control of the vehicle, and the ontology reads 'the driver' through the vehicle's controlled motion, so the duty binds that vehicle. Its class is the admitted aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom and never expanded into the classes it covers; the mapping index maps the same words to the same atom.

'within an intersection' is rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (roadway, shoulder, sidewalk, intersection, ...)', on a region of kind st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges'. rel.occupies is the anchor that makes the junction the subject's own and the kind-ranging relation the region quantifier needs; st.intersection is not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line, and none is read here. The junction this element binds is the one every later condition of this node reads, the intention's target included.

'any vehicle' is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines, the admitted aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom for the road users quantified over inside the obligation. 'approaching from the opposite direction' is read as the ontology directs, since rel.oncoming is 'not a stand-in for the direction a road user approaches from -- that is read through the carrier it approaches through, any carrier st.lane_enters admits ..., whose entrance end is the intersection, and through that carrier's direction (st.lane_direction) at the same instant': the other vehicle occupies (rel.occupies) a carrier of kind st.travel_region whose entrance end is the junction t1 binds (st.lane_enters), and that carrier's designated direction is opposed to the direction of the carrier by which the subject came to the junction, their normalised dot product lying at or below the negative of p.same_direction_cosine_tolerance. This reading is what the words need here, because the subject's own heading swings through the turn while the direction it approached from does not change. 'which is within the intersection' is rel.occupies on the same st.intersection region. 'shall yield the right-of-way' is DEF-NRS-484A-210's right 'to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another vehicle ... unless one grants precedence to the other': the subject grants precedence by not coming into contact with that vehicle (rel.contact, 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap') and by not letting its closest approach to it fall below the clearance, which prim.closest_approach_within and prim.closest_approach_distance give under constant velocities within the horizon and rel.surface_gap measures between the nearest points of the two bodies, with kin.speed the subject's own speed. rel.surface_gap is not read as an order of arrival; rel.contact is not a stand-in for a near miss, which is why the primitives stand beside it.

operationalizations.standard: or so close thereto as to constitute an immediate hazard
operationalizations.convention: Gap-acceptance convention for a left turn across an opposing stream. 'So close thereto' is the oncoming vehicle's distance to the junction, which st.region_geometry gives as 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it'; the hazard is read by the degree to which the words hold, the distance divided by nothing but carried as a product -- the vehicle is so close where that distance is at most its own speed (kin.speed) times p.yield_headway_time, so a faster approach makes a greater distance count and a slower one a smaller. The immediacy of the hazard is read in the same breath by the conflict-avoidance convention: the closest approach between the two bodies under constant velocities within p.yield_conflict_horizon falling below p.yield_min_clearance, measured between the nearest points of the bodies by rel.surface_gap. Both bounds are the reading's, set from gap-acceptance tables for a permitted left turn, and neither is a figure of the law's.

intentions.meaning: the source's current plan for the road user is that it turn to the left at the region named as the declaration's target

applicability: The subject vehicle's footprint overlaps an intersection and the source declares its current plan to be a left turn at that intersection. The declaration is read at the judged observation or earlier, never ahead of it, and the act of turning is not what engages the rule: an intention the plan still holds engages it even while the vehicle waits.
obligation: At every such observation the subject must grant precedence to every vehicle of the aggregate that occupies a carrier whose entrance end is that intersection and whose designated direction is opposed to the direction of the subject's own approach carrier, and that either lies within the intersection or is so close to it as to constitute an immediate hazard -- its distance to the junction region at most its speed times p.yield_headway_time, or its closest approach to the subject under constant velocities within p.yield_conflict_horizon below p.yield_min_clearance. Granting precedence is: no contact with that vehicle, and no closest approach to it within p.yield_conflict_horizon below p.yield_min_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'shall yield the right-of-way' is read as granting precedence in the two observable ways open to a vehicle already within the junction: no contact with the oncoming vehicle, and no closest approach within the horizon closer than the clearance. A deference that shows in neither is outside what a trace can check; the duty is not read as a prohibition on turning at all, which the words do not state.

'approaching from the opposite direction' is read through the designated direction of the carrier by which each vehicle reaches the junction, not through the two bodies' current headings: the subject's heading swings through the turn while the direction it approached from does not, and the ontology directs this reading for exactly these words.
'The driver of a vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: who or what is at the controls is not observable, and the duty binds that vehicle's conduct.

'Its closest approach to it' is read as: the centres approach each other within p.yield_conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within), and at that approach either the centre distance (prim.closest_approach_distance) or the gap between the nearest points of the two bodies (rel.surface_gap, the measure the convention names) lies below p.yield_min_clearance. Where no approach of the centres falls within the horizon the clearance is not read as lost: two bodies drawing apart are no failure to grant precedence, and contact is read beside this by rel.contact.

'The carrier by which the subject came to the junction' is read existentially: some carrier of kind st.travel_region that the subject occupies and whose entrance end is that junction. The ontology fixes a road user's approach by occupancy and entrance topology, and the words name no further way to single one carrier out.

A carrier read as an approach to the junction is not the junction region itself. The kind the record names, st.travel_region, covers the intersection, but st.lane_enters is the source's record of an approach segment's entrance end and is never recorded on the junction that segment enters ('A carrier enters one intersection at most'), so on the junction region the relation is unrecorded rather than false and asking it there could only add an unknown. The junction is therefore excluded as its own approach carrier, which removes no case that relation could decide and no vehicle the duty could reach.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car stands within a junction with the source declaring its plan to be a left turn there. A van occupies the opposing approach lane, which enters the same junction with the opposite designated direction, and is already within the junction. The car turns across its path and the two bodies touch.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same junction and the same declared left turn, and no other road user anywhere in the scene: nothing is owed precedence, the duty is discharged, and the verdict is decided with the subject alone.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car stands within the junction and the source's current plan for it is to go straight through: no left turn is declared at that junction, so the rule is not engaged even though an opposing van is within the junction.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car within the junction is declared to intend a left turn and a van is on the opposing approach, but the source does not report the designated direction of the van's carrier, so whether it approaches from the opposite direction is unknown and the rule reports unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The oncoming van is not yet within the junction but is fifteen metres from it at 12 m/s, so its distance is under its speed times the headway bound: it is so close as to constitute an immediate hazard. The car turns left in front of it and their closest approach under constant velocities within the horizon falls to half a metre.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The oncoming van is a hundred and fifty metres from the junction at 10 m/s, neither within it nor within the headway bound, and no closest approach within the horizon comes near the clearance: the car completes its left turn with nothing owed precedence.

param_proposals.name: p.same_direction_cosine_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Heading-agreement convention: the cosine of the largest angle between two directions still read as the same direction, set at thirty degrees; its negative is the bound at which two directions are read as opposed.
param_proposals.source: The thirty-degree sector convention used for same-direction and opposed-direction tests in traffic conflict analysis.

param_proposals.name: p.yield_headway_time
param_proposals.convention: Gap-acceptance convention: the headway, at the approaching vehicle's own speed, within which that vehicle is read as so close to the junction as to constitute an immediate hazard, being the time a turning or crossing vehicle needs to clear its path.
param_proposals.source: Critical gap and follow-up headway practice for permitted left turns and crossing manoeuvres (Highway Capacity Manual).

param_proposals.name: p.yield_conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: Conflict-avoidance convention: the time ahead of the observation over which a closest approach under constant velocities is read as the 'danger of a crash' the right-of-way definition names, rather than as a passing of two road users on diverging paths.
param_proposals.source: Surrogate-safety practice for time-to-conflict measures at junctions (post-encroachment and time-to-collision thresholds of two to three seconds).

param_proposals.name: p.yield_min_clearance
param_proposals.convention: Conflict-avoidance convention: the clearance between the nearest points of two bodies below which a closest approach is read as a failure to grant precedence rather than as a safe passing.
param_proposals.source: Lateral and longitudinal clearance practice for passing a road user at low speed in a junction.

segmentation.text: It is unlawful for any person to drive or operate a vehicle of any kind or character at:
A rate of speed greater than that posted by a public authority for the particular portion of highway being traversed.

elements.justification: The same words as in NRS_484B_600_1a and read the same way: 'a vehicle of any kind or character' is the defined term the table resolves to DEF-NRS-484A-320, admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, and ru.aggregate carries 'membership of a legal aggregate ... the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id'; 'to drive or operate' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, drv.motion.standstill ('the road user is motionless at the observation: the magnitude of its velocity is at most the speed tolerance') read negated, a vehicle in motion being taken to be driven. Exclusions: ru.aggregate is not a stand-in for a class atom or a relational role; drv.motion.standstill is not a stand-in for the engine being off or a brake being applied, neither of which is read.

kin.speed, 'magnitude of velocity', is the 'rate of speed'. dev.speed_limit_sign is a 'sign stating a maximum or minimum speed, with value and unit; kind in {maximum, minimum, structure_maximum, zone}', and its value for a sign of kind maximum, structure_maximum or zone is the speed 'posted ... for the particular portion of highway being traversed'. dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls -- a lane, reserved lane, turn lane, centre turn lane, bicycle lane or path, roadway, one-way roadway or shoulder -- or an intersection', ties the sign to that portion: a travel region the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'), quantified over st.travel_region, the kind dev.governs ranges over. st.on_way, 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on', and st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines', carry 'of highway'. Exclusions: dev.governs is 'not a stand-in for a position', so dev.position is not read and no distance to the sign head is used; a sign of kind minimum is not read, the words forbidding only a speed greater than the posted one; st.travel_region is 'not a stand-in for the extent of a highway', which its own atom carries.

applicability: The subject vehicle v is in motion at the observation (drv.motion.standstill false for v, with p.standstill_speed_tolerance), which is how 'to drive or operate' is read, and some dev.speed_limit_sign of kind maximum, structure_maximum or zone governs (dev.governs) a travel region v's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies), that region lying on a highway (st.on_way, st.highway). Where no such sign governs a region v occupies, the duty does not arise.
obligation: v's speed (kin.speed) is at most the value of every such posted maximum: for each dev.speed_limit_sign of kind maximum, structure_maximum or zone governing a travel region v occupies, kin.speed does not exceed that sign's stated value, so the lowest posted maximum binds.

narrowings.why: 'for any person to drive or operate' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, as the ontology's section on what is not an atom directs: a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven, and the duty binds that vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.

'posted by a public authority' is read as the presence of the speed-limit sign on the road: the feature's presence is the observable evidence of its official posting, as the ontology directs for the legal status of a feature on the road. Which authority posted it, and its jurisdiction under DEF-NRS-484A-195, are not read.

'the particular portion of highway being traversed' is read as a travel region the vehicle's footprint overlaps whose traffic the sign governs (dev.governs), that region lying on a highway; where several such signs govern regions the vehicle occupies, the lowest posted maximum binds. The posted maximum is read from signs of kind maximum, structure_maximum and zone, and a speed-limit sign carries no conditions attribute, so a legend stating hours or a class is read as a posting in effect.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A maximum-kind speed-limit sign governs the lane the subject occupies; the subject runs along that lane at a speed above the sign's stated value.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same lane and the same governing maximum-kind sign; the subject's speed stays below the sign's stated value throughout. No other road user is present in the scene.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject runs along a highway on which the source records the governance of every device and no speed-limit sign governs any region the subject occupies, so no posted limit applies to the portion traversed.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject runs fast along a lane beside a sign head the source records, but the source does not observe speed-limit signs or their stated values, so whether a posted maximum is exceeded cannot be told.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Two signs govern regions the subject occupies, a maximum-kind sign on the roadway and a lower zone-kind sign on the lane; the subject's speed lies between the two values, above the lower posted maximum.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A minimum-kind speed-limit sign governs the lane the subject occupies and no other speed-limit sign does; the subject runs faster than that sign's stated value, which the words do not reach.

param_proposals.name: p.standstill_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Standstill convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed reading is read as the definition's complete cessation from movement, the bound within which measurement error and sampling cannot be told from no movement at all.
param_proposals.source: the speed resolution of vehicle-dynamics and scene-graph sources, of the order of a tenth of a metre per second.

segmentation.text: It is unlawful for any person to drive or operate a vehicle of any kind or character at:
A rate of speed greater than
is reasonable or proper, having due regard for the traffic, surface and width of the highway, the weather and other highway conditions.

elements.justification: 'a vehicle of any kind or character' is the defined term the table resolves to DEF-NRS-484A-320, admitted as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, and ru.aggregate carries 'membership of a legal aggregate ... the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id'; 'of any kind or character' adds no member the definition does not carry, the definition itself reaching 'every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway' with its four exceptions. 'to drive or operate' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, for which drv.motion.standstill ('the road user is motionless at the observation: the magnitude of its velocity is at most the speed tolerance') is read negated: a vehicle in motion is taken to be driven. Exclusions: ru.aggregate is not a stand-in for a class atom or for a relational role such as who controls the vehicle; drv.motion.standstill is 'not a stand-in for ... the engine being off or a brake being applied', none of which is read here.

kin.speed is the 'magnitude of velocity' in m/s, which is the 'rate of speed' the words compare; 'greater than' is the comparison of that magnitude with the bound the standard of s3 sets. Exclusion: kin.speed is the magnitude and not the acceleration along heading (kin.accel_longitudinal), which is not read.

operationalizations.standard: a rate of speed greater than is reasonable or proper, having due regard for the traffic, surface and width of the highway, the weather and other highway conditions
operationalizations.convention: A stopping-sight-distance and surface-friction reading of a reasonable speed. A base design speed stands for a dry, wide, level and unobstructed stretch; it is lowered by the wet-pavement decrement where the surface is wet or precipitation falls and by the larger winter-surface decrement where the surface is icy or snow-covered; by the per-user traffic decrement for each road user of the scene whose footprint lies on the highway the subject occupies, so the bound falls as the stream thickens; and by the grade decrement times the magnitude of the longitudinal slope at the subject's place, the braking-distance model's grade correction. The speed is bounded in addition by the shortest available sight: the sight distance of the subject's place and the visibility distance, each divided by the perception-reaction-plus-braking time of the stopping-distance model, and by the width of the lane the subject occupies divided by the lateral-recovery time of the lane-keeping convention, so that a narrower lane bounds the speed in proportion to its width. Values come from the AASHTO Green Book's design-speed, stopping-sight-distance and grade-correction tables and from the wet- and winter-surface practice of the same standard.

applicability: The subject vehicle v is in motion at the observation (drv.motion.standstill false for v, with p.standstill_speed_tolerance), which is how 'to drive or operate' is read: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever is at the controls.
obligation: v's speed (kin.speed) does not exceed the reasonable-speed bound: p.reasonable_speed_base_limit lowered by p.reasonable_speed_wet_decrement where env.wet_road or env.precipitation holds, by p.reasonable_speed_ice_decrement where env.ice_or_snow holds, by p.reasonable_speed_traffic_decrement_per_user for each road user of the scene whose footprint overlaps the st.highway region v occupies, and by p.reasonable_speed_grade_decrement_per_unit_grade times the magnitude of st.grade at v's place; and in no case above st.lane_width of the lane v occupies divided by p.reasonable_speed_lane_width_time, st.sight_distance of v's place divided by p.reasonable_speed_sight_time, or env.visibility divided by p.reasonable_speed_sight_time. The standard is the whole obligation, so the node is a surrogate: its verdicts are evidence, not a legal conclusion.

narrowings.why: 'for any person to drive or operate' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, as the ontology's section on what is not an atom directs: a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven, and the duty binds that vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it. No person, no control of a vehicle and no operation is read as such.

'the traffic' is read as the count of the road users of the scene whose footprint overlaps the highway the subject occupies, each lowering the bound by the per-user decrement. The term's definition, DEF-NRS-484A-285, reaches 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel', which is every road user a scene carries, so presence on the way reads the stream; 'for purposes of travel' is read as that presence, no purpose being observable. The operationalization bounds the standard with atoms and primitives, so no aggregate membership is claimed for the count, and a member the scene does not carry as a road user is not counted.

'surface' and 'the weather' are read through the contracts the ontology carries for them -- a wet surface, falling precipitation, ice or snow, and the visibility distance -- the first three selecting a decrement and the last entering the bound by its magnitude. A surface defect, a loose or unpaved surface, and wind are carried by no contract and are not read.

'width of the highway' is read as the width of the lane the subject occupies, divided by the lateral-recovery time; the whole width between the highway's boundary lines carries no atom of its own, and the lane's width is the width the vehicle runs in. The reading is narrower than the words.

'other highway conditions', the standard's catch-all, is read only through the longitudinal slope at the vehicle's place (st.grade), the sight distance of that place (st.sight_distance) and the visibility distance (env.visibility); further conditions the catch-all covers are not read.

The standard's conditions are read at the regions the subject occupies and that lie on the highway it occupies: the longitudinal slope (st.grade) and the sight distance (st.sight_distance) at the roadway region, read as 'the subject's place', and the width (st.lane_width) at the lane region, read as the 'width of the highway' the record narrows to the lane the vehicle runs in. The record names st.highway, st.roadway, st.lane and st.on_way without saying which region carries which figure; this is the assignment chosen.

'the highway' and 'the lane' are definite in the words; where more than one occupied region of a kind qualifies, the bound is required at every one of them (a universal over the selected regions) rather than at one of them, which is the stricter of the readings the words allow.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: On a wet two-lane highway with a short sight distance at the subject's place and a file of other road users on the same way, the subject runs at a speed far above the base limit, let alone the lowered bound and the sight-derived bounds.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A dry, level, wide stretch with a long sight distance, good visibility and no other road user in the scene; the subject runs at a speed well below the base limit and below every sight- and width-derived bound.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject stands at the kerb with its engine running, the magnitude of its velocity within the standstill tolerance, so it is not driven or operated and the duty does not arise.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject runs on a dry, level, wide stretch at a speed below the base limit, the traffic count and the place's sight distance recorded, but the source declares the visibility distance absent, so whether the visibility-derived bound is exceeded cannot be told.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A dry, level, straight stretch with a long sight distance and no other road user in the scene, but the lane the subject occupies is a narrow one: the subject's speed exceeds the lane's width divided by the lateral-recovery time while staying below the base limit.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A dry stretch running down a steep grade with no other road user present; the subject's speed stays below the base limit but above that limit lowered by the grade decrement times the magnitude of the slope at its place.

param_proposals.name: p.standstill_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Standstill convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed reading is read as the definition's complete cessation from movement, the bound within which measurement error and sampling cannot be told from no movement at all.
param_proposals.source: the speed resolution of vehicle-dynamics and scene-graph sources, of the order of a tenth of a metre per second.

param_proposals.name: p.reasonable_speed_base_limit
param_proposals.convention: Design-speed convention: the speed a dry, wide, level, straight and unobstructed open-road stretch supports, before any correction for surface, stream, slope or sight; it is the upper anchor of the reasonable-speed bound and is lowered by every factor the standard names.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book design-speed table for rural arterial highways (the 65 mph design speed).

param_proposals.name: p.reasonable_speed_wet_decrement
param_proposals.convention: Wet-pavement convention: the reduction from the dry design speed that keeps the braking distance of the stopping-distance model unchanged on a wet surface, about a tenth of the design speed.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book wet-pavement friction factors used in the stopping-sight-distance model.

param_proposals.name: p.reasonable_speed_ice_decrement
param_proposals.convention: Winter-surface convention: the larger reduction from the dry design speed that keeps the braking distance unchanged on an icy or snow-covered surface, whose friction is a small fraction of the dry value.
param_proposals.source: winter maintenance practice and the low-friction end of the AASHTO braking-distance model.

param_proposals.name: p.reasonable_speed_traffic_decrement_per_user
param_proposals.convention: Traffic-density convention: the reduction of the bound for each road user of the scene present on the highway the subject occupies, so that the bound falls as the stream thickens and the space to react shortens.
param_proposals.source: the speed-flow relations of the Highway Capacity Manual, whose free-flow speed falls steadily as flow on a segment rises.

param_proposals.name: p.reasonable_speed_grade_decrement_per_unit_grade
param_proposals.convention: Grade-correction convention: the reduction of the bound per unit of longitudinal slope magnitude, taken from the grade correction of the braking-distance model, so that a few per cent of slope costs a little over a metre per second.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book stopping-sight-distance tables with grade corrections for downgrades.

param_proposals.name: p.reasonable_speed_lane_width_time
param_proposals.convention: Lateral-recovery convention: the time within which a driver must correct a lateral excursion of the order of the lane's width; dividing the lane width by it turns the width into a speed bound, so that a narrower lane bounds the speed in proportion to its width and a standard lane yields a bound near the open-road design speed.
param_proposals.source: lane-keeping and lateral-recovery times of vehicle-dynamics practice, calibrated against the standard 3.6 m lane and the design speed.

param_proposals.name: p.reasonable_speed_sight_time
param_proposals.convention: Stopping-sight-distance convention: the perception-reaction plus braking time over which the available sight must cover the distance the vehicle travels; dividing the place's sight distance, or the visibility distance, by it gives the speed at which the vehicle can still stop within what can be seen.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book brake-reaction time of 2.5 s used in the stopping-sight-distance model.

segmentation.text: If the driver of a vehicle
intends to turn
at an intersection and:
Both intersecting highways are two-directional:
The approach for a left turn must be made in that portion of the right half of the highway nearest the centerline thereof.

elements.justification: 'the driver of a vehicle' binds the subject: DEF-NRS-484A-080 makes the driver the one who drives or is in actual physical control of the vehicle, and the ontology reads 'the driver' through the vehicle's controlled motion, so the duty binds that vehicle, of the admitted aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway, except ...'), claimed as one atom and never expanded. The mapping index maps 'The driver of a vehicle' to the same atom.

'at an intersection' names the place the turn is intended at and the junction the approach leads to: st.intersection is 'the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges', st.lane_enters 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end', st.travel_region the kind that carrier quantifier ranges over, and rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') the anchor that makes the junction the one the subject itself approaches. This element binds the region the declared intention of the preceding span is read at, and the same region the obligation's approach leads into. The trailing 'and:' only joins this condition to the next.

'two-directional' is the term DEF-NRS-484B-073 defines, used here in the copular form rather than as one contiguous phrase: 'an undivided highway upon which vehicles are allowed to proceed in opposite directions'. 'undivided' is the absence of st.median_or_divider, 'physical barrier or dividing section between roadways', on that way; 'upon which vehicles are allowed to proceed in opposite directions' is read from the designated directions of the carriers the way carries: st.lane_direction, 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in -- a lane, reserved lane, turn lane, bicycle lane or path, or a roadway, one-way roadway or shoulder', opposed between two carriers of the way, their normalised dot product at or below the negative of p.same_direction_cosine_tolerance. st.highway is the way itself as DEF-NRS-484A-095 defines it, 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority', st.roadway 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder', and st.on_way 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on', which ties each carrier and each divider to its way. 'Both intersecting highways' are the two ways meeting at the junction the previous span binds: st.intersection with st.on_way, since 'an intersection lies on every way that meets there', and st.lane_enters with st.travel_region and rel.occupies pick out the subject's own way among them. st.median_or_divider is not read as a lane marking, and st.lane_direction is not read as a road user's heading.

'The approach for a left turn must be made in' is the subject's lateral place while it occupies the carrier whose entrance end is that junction: rel.occupies is the anchor, st.travel_region the kind the carrier quantifier ranges over, st.lane_enters the entrance relation and st.intersection the junction. 'that portion of the right half of the highway nearest the centerline thereof' is read in the two ways the ontology provides for a way with and without marked lanes. Where the carriageway is laned, st.lane is 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles' and st.lane_adjacency carries the 'lane ordinal within the carriageway and the count of lanes in that direction; ordinal 1 is the leftmost lane, looking along the lane's direction': on a two-directional highway the leftmost lane of the subject's direction, read along st.lane_direction, is the portion of the right half nearest the centre line, so ordinal 1 for that direction is the portion the words name. Where no lane is recorded, st.centre_line is 'the marking, or the geometric centre, dividing the two directions of a two-way roadway' and prim.region_lateral_offset gives 'the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user': the centre line lies to the subject's left, its offset positive and of magnitude at least p.lateral_offset_resolution, which places the subject on the right half, and at most p.centerline_adjacent_distance, which is the portion nearest the centre line. st.roadway, st.highway and st.on_way bind the way and its improved part; st.lane_adjacency is expressly not a stand-in for the marking between two lanes, and none is read as one; st.lane is not a stand-in for a half of the roadway, which is why the unlaned case is read through the centre line and the lateral offset rather than through a lane ordinal; the primitive's own inputs are not claimed beside it.

intentions.meaning: the source's current plan for the road user is that it turn to the left at the region named as the declaration's target

applicability: The subject vehicle occupies a carrier whose entrance end is an intersection; the source declares its current plan to be a left turn at that intersection; and both the way carrying that carrier and the other way meeting at that junction are two-directional -- no physical barrier or dividing section lies on either, and each carries two carriers whose designated directions are opposed.
obligation: At every observation on that approach the subject must lie in the portion of the right half of its highway nearest the centre line: it occupies the lane of ordinal 1 for its own direction of travel, counted along that lane's designated direction, or, where the carriageway carries no recorded lane, the centre line of its roadway lies to its left with a signed lateral offset of at least p.lateral_offset_resolution and at most p.centerline_adjacent_distance.

narrowings.why: 'The approach for a left turn' restricts the duty to an approach made for a turn to the left: the condition span carries a declared intention to turn, and the obligation's own words select the left turn among the turns the earlier words allow, so the duty is read only where the declaration is a left turn at that junction.

'that portion of the right half of the highway nearest the centerline thereof' is read, where the carriageway is laned, as the lane of ordinal 1 for the subject's direction -- the leftmost lane of that direction and so the one adjoining the centre line -- and, where no lane is recorded, as a place whose signed lateral offset to the centre line is positive and at most p.centerline_adjacent_distance. The second bound is a width the reading sets, since the words name a portion and no measure of it; it is set at a design lane width, so that the portion read is the width of one line of vehicles beside the centre line.

'are allowed to proceed in opposite directions' is read as the designated directions of the carriers the way carries being opposed: a permission granted by an authority is nothing a scene displays, and the designated direction of travel on the road is its observable evidence.
'the driver of a vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: who or what is at the controls is not observable, and the duty binds that vehicle's conduct.

'that portion of the right half of the highway nearest the centerline thereof' is written, where the carrier is a recorded lane, as the lane with no neighbouring lane of its own direction on its left: st.lane_adjacency counts ordinals from the left looking along the lane's designated direction, so the leftmost lane of that direction is the record's ordinal 1, and the relation states it without a magnitude of this file's own.

'where the carriageway carries no recorded lane' is written as the approach carrier the subject occupies not being a recorded lane (st.lane): the duty is read carrier by carrier, so the centre-line reading applies exactly at a carrier whose lanes the source does not record.

'The approach for a left turn must be made in' is read at every carrier the subject occupies whose entrance end is that junction, not at one of them: where it occupies several, no carrier that favours the subject is picked.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A four-lane undivided street, two lanes each way, meets another undivided two-way street. The source declares the car's plan to be a left turn at that junction, and the car runs the whole approach in the kerbside lane -- ordinal 2 of its direction -- up to the junction.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same geometry and the same declared left turn. The car runs the approach in the lane of ordinal 1 for its direction, the one adjoining the centre line, throughout. No other road user is in the scene and the verdict is decided.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The car approaches the same junction in the kerbside lane, but the source's current plan for it is to go straight through: no left turn is declared at that junction, so the rule is not engaged.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The car approaches the junction with a declared left turn, but the source does not report the lane ordinals of the carriageway and the roadway carries a recorded lane, so which portion of the right half the car occupies is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A narrow two-way street with no lanes recorded, meeting another undivided two-way street. The car, declared to turn left at the junction, runs the approach with the centre line two metres to its left, inside the centre-line portion.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The car, declared to turn left, approaches a junction on a highway divided by a raised median: the way is not two-directional in the definition's sense, so this paragraph does not apply.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: An unlaned two-way street, the car declared to turn left at the junction, running the whole approach close to the kerb with the centre line six metres to its left, outside the centre-line portion.

param_proposals.name: p.same_direction_cosine_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Heading-agreement convention: the cosine of the largest angle between two directions still read as the same direction, set at thirty degrees; its negative is the bound at which two directions are read as opposed.
param_proposals.source: The thirty-degree sector convention used for same-direction and opposed-direction tests in traffic conflict analysis.

param_proposals.name: p.lateral_offset_resolution
param_proposals.convention: Lateral-offset convention: the magnitude of a signed lateral offset below which the side a region lies on is not distinguishable from the measurement noise of the boundary and the position.
param_proposals.source: Map and localisation practice for boundary polygons in scene-graph traces.

param_proposals.name: p.centerline_adjacent_distance
param_proposals.convention: Lane-position convention: the lateral distance from the centre line within which a place on the right half of a two-directional highway counts as the portion nearest the centre line, set at one design lane width, the width of a single line of vehicles beside the centre line.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book design lane widths for urban arterials (3.0 to 3.6 m).

segmentation.text: Every vehicle driven upon a divided highway
must be driven only upon the right-hand roadway
and must not be driven over, across or within any dividing space, barrier or section or make any left turn, semicircular turn or U-turn,
except through an opening in the barrier or dividing section or space or at a crossover or intersection established by a public authority.

elements.justification: “vehicle” is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines and the run admits as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as ru.aggregate with that id. “a divided highway” is DEF-NRS-484A-070, “a highway divided into two or more roadways by means of a physical barrier or dividing section”: st.highway is the way, st.median_or_divider the “physical barrier or dividing section between roadways; opening attribute where a crossover exists”, st.roadway the part improved for vehicular traffic, whose contract states that “separate roadways of a divided highway are separate”, and st.on_way what makes them parts of one way. rel.occupies anchors the way to the subject, and the negation of drv.motion.standstill carries “driven” as controlled motion (narrowing on this span).

“driven over, across or within any dividing space, barrier or section” is the overlap of the vehicle's footprint with st.median_or_divider, the “physical barrier or dividing section between roadways”, read through rel.occupies, “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (… median …)”: over, across and within are all the overlap of the body with that region, there being no observable difference between driving over a dividing section and being within it at an observation. “any left turn” is drv.motion.left_turn, the turn to the left recognized when the heading change accumulated since the onset of the turn reaches the turn angle, and “U-turn” is drv.motion.u_turn, which carries the posted definition DEF-NRS-484B-077, “the turning of a vehicle upon a highway so as to proceed in the opposite direction, whether accomplished by one continuous movement or not”; both read kin.yaw_rate, “rate of change of heading, positive when the heading turns to the left”, whose exclusion of road curvature does not apply because the body's yaw and not the road's bend is read. st.highway with st.on_way and rel.occupies carries “upon a highway” in the U-turn definition for the way the vehicle is on. “semicircular turn” is read through the same two concepts (narrowing on this span).

“an opening in the barrier or dividing section or space” and “a crossover” are st.median_or_divider's own “opening attribute where a crossover exists”, so the atom carries both; “or intersection” is st.intersection, “the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges”. rel.occupies anchors the opening or junction to the subject and st.on_way ties it to the same divided highway. “established by a public authority” is read through the presence of the feature (narrowing on this span).

applicability: The bound road user is a vehicle of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle that is moving and whose footprint overlaps a highway on which a dividing space, barrier or section separates two or more roadways: a divided highway.
obligation: At no observation may the vehicle (a) have its footprint overlapping the dividing space, barrier or section of that way (rel.occupies on st.median_or_divider), or (b) be recognized as having made a left turn (drv.motion.left_turn with p.turn_onset_yaw_rate, p.left_turn_angle and p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph) or a turn reversing its direction of travel (drv.motion.u_turn with p.turn_onset_yaw_rate, p.u_turn_reversal_angle and the same step bound) upon that way. The exception of s4 excuses an act only where the vehicle's footprint overlaps an opening in the barrier or dividing section, a crossover or an intersection on that way throughout the act — from the onset of the turn to its recognition — so a turn begun at an opening and completed on the travelled roadway beyond it is not excused. Where the yaw rate since the onset, the divider's region or the vehicle's occupancy of the opening is unobserved, the duty is unknown.

onset.words: the observation at which the vehicle's rate of change of heading first rose above the onset yaw rate, counted from zero at that observation
onset.justification: kin.yaw_rate is “rate of change of heading, positive when the heading turns to the left, in deg/s”, which is the quantity whose rise marks the beginning of the turning; its exclusion “not a stand-in for road curvature — a vehicle yaws on a straight road whenever it manoeuvres” is why the onset is read from the body's yaw and not from the road, and the same atom is what the accumulated heading change since that onset is integrated from.

occasion.recognition: the observation at which the heading change accumulated since that onset first reaches the turn angle of the left-turn concept, or the reversal angle of the U-turn concept

under_way.words: the vehicle's rate of change of heading stands above the onset yaw rate, or the heading change accumulated since the onset stands clear of zero, at the observation
under_way.justification: An observation inside the act is told from one before it began by the vehicle's own motion: kin.yaw_rate, “rate of change of heading, positive when the heading turns to the left”, is above the onset rate while the body is turning, and the heading change integrated from the same atom since the onset is non-zero from the onset on, whereas before the onset no such accumulation exists. No region or place is read, since the vehicle occupied the same roadway and the same way before the turn began.

narrowings.why: “Every vehicle driven upon a divided highway” is read as the vehicle whose motion is controlled: who or what controls a road user is not observable, and the ontology reads “drives” and “driven” through the vehicle's controlled motion.

“semicircular turn” is read through the same two concepts as the other turns the span names: a turn through a half circle is a turn whose heading change reaches the reversal angle, which is what the U-turn concept recognizes, and one made to the left also reaches the left-turn angle. No separate concept is proposed, because a semicircular turn differs from the reversal the U-turn definition states only in the path's shape, which no contract of the vocabulary tells apart from the heading change, and the span names both words as members of one list of prohibited turns.

“driven over, across or within” is read as the overlap of the vehicle's footprint with the dividing space, barrier or section at the observation. The three prepositions name one observable fact — the body on that region — since a body that is driven over or across a dividing section overlaps it at some observation of the crossing, and no contract distinguishes passing over it from standing within it.

“established by a public authority” is read as the presence of the opening, crossover or junction on the road. That a feature is official or designated by an authority is a legal status the ontology reads through the feature itself: its presence is the evidence of that status.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: On a divided highway with a kerbed central dividing section, a car running at 12 m/s swings to the left: its yaw rate rises well above the onset rate, and about two seconds later the heading change accumulated since that onset passes the left-turn angle while its footprint overlaps the dividing section. No opening, crossover or junction covers any observation of the turn.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same car runs straight along the nearside roadway of the divided highway for the whole recording: its yaw rate never rises above the onset rate, no heading change accumulates, and its footprint never overlaps the central dividing section.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car makes a U-turn on a two-lane undivided highway with a painted centre line and no physical barrier or dividing section. The way is not a divided highway and the rule does not engage.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The forbid scene with the source declaring the yaw rate of road users absent: the divided highway, the dividing section and the car's track are recorded, but no heading change can be integrated, so whether a left turn or a reversal was made is unknown and the duty is unknown.

scenarios.name: occasion_s4
scenarios.narrative: The car begins a U-turn inside a crossover recorded as an opening in the central dividing section: at the onset and for the first second its footprint overlaps the opening, but it swings wide and completes the reversal with its body on the travelled roadway beyond the opening, where the heading change reaches the reversal angle. The exception holds for part of the act only, and a part-covered act is not excused.

scenarios.name: occasion_s4_outside
scenarios.narrative: The car runs along the nearside roadway, its body clear of any opening, and then turns left into a junction established on that way: from the onset of the turn to the observation at which the heading change reaches the turn angle its footprint overlaps that junction region throughout, although it did not before the turn began. The exception covers the whole act and the duty does not bite on it.

param_proposals.name: p.standstill_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Standstill convention: the speed at or below which a sampled reading is read as a complete cessation from movement, set at the noise floor of vehicle speed measurement.
param_proposals.source: stop-detection thresholds used in naturalistic-driving data reduction

param_proposals.name: p.turn_onset_yaw_rate
param_proposals.convention: Manoeuvre-onset convention: the rate of change of heading above which a body is read as turning rather than running straight with sensor noise and small corrections, which fixes the observed beginning from which a turn's heading change is counted.
param_proposals.source: yaw-rate onset thresholds in manoeuvre-segmentation practice

param_proposals.name: p.left_turn_angle
param_proposals.convention: Turn-recognition convention: the heading change accumulated since the onset at which a turn to the left is recognized as a turn rather than a lane change or a curve, taken from the smallest angle a junction turn subtends.
param_proposals.source: turn-classification angle thresholds in trajectory-based manoeuvre recognition

param_proposals.name: p.u_turn_reversal_angle
param_proposals.convention: Reversal convention: the accumulated heading change at which the definition's proceeding in the opposite direction is recognized, set below a half turn so that a reversal completed between sampled observations or on a skewed way is still recognized.
param_proposals.source: U-turn detection angle thresholds in trajectory-based manoeuvre recognition

segmentation.text: Except when traffic is being controlled by a police officer or a traffic-control signal:

When proper signs have been erected, the driver of a vehicle shall stop or yield at a clearly marked stop line or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is none, then at the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.
After having stopped or, in the event of a yield sign, slowed or stopped,
the driver
shall yield the right-of-way to other vehicles which have entered the intersection from such through highway
or which are approaching so closely on such through highway as to constitute an immediate hazard
during the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection.

elements.justification: The same words as in the first node of this line take the same atoms. 'traffic' is DEF-NRS-484A-285's aggregate, claimed as the single atom ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic. 'being controlled by a police officer' is dev.human_direction, 'a person directing traffic and the direction given', with role police_officer, which is DEF-NRS-484A-180's 'officer authorized to direct or regulate traffic'; 'or a traffic-control signal' is dev.traffic_signal, 'a signal head', the device by which traffic is alternately directed to stop or proceed. The controlling is dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection', read on the junction the subject is at or on its own approach carrier, which rel.occupies, st.travel_region, st.lane_enters and st.intersection bind.

'After having stopped or, in the event of a yield sign, slowed or stopped' refers to the act the first sentence of the subsection requires, and the condition carries it with every qualification the referring words keep: the same subject, the same place, the same choice of act under a yield sign, and the order before the crossing. The halt is drv.motion.standstill, DEF-NRS-484A-255's 'complete cessation from movement' within the speed tolerance its contract names; 'slowed' is kin.speed, 'magnitude of velocity', at or below p.yield_sign_slowed_max_speed, which is owed only where dev.yield_sign ('regulatory sign requiring yielding without a mandatory halt') and not dev.stop_sign governs the subject's approach carrier, dev.governs giving 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'. The place is carried as the first sentence states it: st.stop_line ('the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device') or st.crosswalk, each tied to the subject's own entrance by st.entrance_of and st.lane_enters, with st.travel_region the kind the carrier quantifier ranges over and rel.occupies the anchor; else the point at which st.sight_along_way reaches the view distance on the way st.on_way and st.highway bind. prim.region_offset_along gives the side along st.lane_direction and st.region_geometry the distance between the body and the mark that the stop-point tolerance bounds. A weaker fact -- a halt anywhere, or a slowing under a stop sign -- is not the act the words refer to, so the full qualification is carried here; the defining words are marked sibling only because the duty they state belongs to the other node.

'the driver' is the driver of the same vehicle the first sentence binds; the ontology reads 'the driver' through the vehicle's controlled motion, so the duty binds that vehicle, of the admitted aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom.

'other vehicles' are road users of the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines, the admitted aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom and quantified over inside the obligation. 'which have entered the intersection' is drv.motion.region_entry ('comes to overlap a structure region at the observation') on the junction region of kind st.intersection, with rel.occupies for their lying within it since. 'from such through highway' reads the way of the carrier each entered by: st.lane_enters gives the carrier whose entrance end is that junction, st.travel_region the kind that quantifier ranges over, st.on_way 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on' and st.highway the way itself; that way is the crossing highway at whose entrance the subject's own governing sign stands, which dev.stop_sign, dev.yield_sign and dev.governs identify -- DEF-NRS-484A-275 makes a through highway one at whose entrances traffic must yield in obedience to such a sign, and the sign governing the subject's approach is that designation's observable evidence. 'shall yield the right-of-way' is DEF-NRS-484A-210's right 'to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another vehicle ... unless one grants precedence to the other': the subject grants precedence by not coming into contact with such a vehicle (rel.contact, 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap') and by not letting its closest approach to it fall below the clearance, which prim.closest_approach_within and prim.closest_approach_distance give under constant velocities within the horizon and rel.surface_gap measures between the nearest points of the bodies, with kin.speed the subject's own speed. rel.surface_gap is not read as an order of arrival, which the other vehicle's entry event carries.

'during the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection' fixes when the duty is read: rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') on the junction region of kind st.intersection gives the subject's being across or within it, and kin.speed, 'magnitude of velocity', above p.standstill_speed_tolerance gives its moving. rel.occupies is the anchor to the subject's own footprint, and st.intersection is not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line: the words name the junction itself.

operationalizations.standard: or which are approaching so closely on such through highway as to constitute an immediate hazard
operationalizations.convention: Gap-acceptance convention for a stop- or yield-controlled crossing. 'So closely' is the other vehicle's distance to the junction, which st.region_geometry gives as 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it', read on a vehicle whose carrier lies on the through highway (rel.occupies, st.travel_region, st.lane_enters, st.on_way, st.highway): the vehicle is so close where that distance is at most its own speed (kin.speed) times p.yield_headway_time, so the bound moves with its speed -- a faster approach makes a greater distance count, a slower one a smaller -- rather than switching on its presence. The immediacy is read in the same breath by the conflict-avoidance convention: the closest approach between the two bodies under constant velocities within p.yield_conflict_horizon falling below p.yield_min_clearance, measured between the nearest points of the bodies by rel.surface_gap. Both figures are the reading's, from gap-acceptance tables for a crossing manoeuvre, and neither is the law's.

applicability: At an earlier observation on the same approach the subject halted at the place the subsection's first sentence names, or, where a yield sign and not a stop sign governs its approach carrier, halted or came down to a speed at or below p.yield_sign_slowed_max_speed there; the subject's footprint now overlaps that intersection and its speed is above p.standstill_speed_tolerance, so that it is moving across or within the junction. The duty does not apply where a police officer is directing the traffic there or a traffic-control signal governs the junction or the approach. The act is searched for back from the subject's entry into the junction as the first node of this line states it; where that history begins before the recording the condition, and so the rule, is unknown.
obligation: At every observation at which the subject is moving across or within that intersection it must grant precedence to every vehicle of the aggregate that has entered the junction from a carrier lying on the through highway, and to every such vehicle on that highway approaching so closely as to constitute an immediate hazard -- its distance to the junction at most its speed times p.yield_headway_time, or its closest approach to the subject under constant velocities within p.yield_conflict_horizon below p.yield_min_clearance. Granting precedence is: no contact with that vehicle, and no closest approach to it within p.yield_conflict_horizon below p.yield_min_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'shall yield the right-of-way' is read as granting precedence in the two observable ways open to a vehicle that is already moving across or within the junction: no contact with the privileged vehicle, and no closest approach within the horizon closer than the clearance. A deference that shows in neither is outside what a trace can check.

'which have entered the intersection' is read as an entry event of that vehicle into the junction at or before the judged observation together with its lying within the junction since: a vehicle that has entered and left no longer competes for the junction.

'such through highway' is read as the crossing highway at whose entrance the stop or yield sign governing the subject's approach stands: the sign's presence is the observable evidence of the designation DEF-NRS-484A-275 describes.

'slowed' under a yield sign is read as a speed at the place at or below p.yield_sign_slowed_max_speed, the sign's own contract requiring 'yielding without a mandatory halt'; the condition is otherwise carried with the place and the order the first sentence gives it.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: who or what is at the controls is not observable, and the duty binds that vehicle's conduct.

'the closest approach ... below p.yield_min_clearance' is read as either the centre distance at the closest approach within p.yield_conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within, prim.closest_approach_distance, which compute on the centres under constant velocities) falling below the clearance, or the gap between the nearest points of the two bodies (rel.surface_gap, the clearance the convention names) falling below it: the primitive gives the approach, the relation the measure between the bodies.

the standard's two figures are read as alternatives, as the node's own obligation states them ('its distance to the junction at most its speed times p.yield_headway_time, or its closest approach to the subject ... below p.yield_min_clearance'): a vehicle on the through highway that meets either is approaching so closely as to constitute an immediate hazard.

scenarios.name: forbid
