scenarios.narrative: A stop sign governs the car's approach lane to a highway junction. The car halts at the stop line, then pulls out and crosses the junction while a van that entered the junction from the highway is within it, and the two bodies touch inside the junction.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same junction and halt at the stop line. The car then crosses the junction and no other road user is in the scene at any observation: nothing has entered from the through highway and nothing approaches on it, so the duty is discharged with the subject alone.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The car never halts and never slows at the stop line: it rolls straight through and across the junction. The condition that it had stopped, or under a yield sign slowed or stopped, does not hold, so this rule is not engaged and only the first node of the line judges the conduct.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The car halts at its stop line and moves into the junction while a van is on the highway, but the source carries no boundary outline for the junction region, so the van's distance to the junction cannot be read and whether it approaches so closely as to be an immediate hazard is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The car halts at its stop line, then pulls across the junction while a van on the through highway is thirty metres away at 25 m/s -- within its speed times the headway bound -- and their closest approach under constant velocities within the horizon falls to a metre: a vehicle approaching so closely as to constitute an immediate hazard is not given precedence.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A yield sign governs the approach. The car slows to 3 m/s at the yield line without halting, which satisfies the condition, and then crosses while the nearest vehicle on the through highway is two hundred metres away at 20 m/s: neither within the headway bound nor near the clearance bound.

param_proposals.name: p.standstill_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Standstill convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed reading is read as the complete cessation from movement DEF-NRS-484A-255 requires, set at the noise floor of a speed channel at rest.
param_proposals.source: Instrumentation practice for speed channels in scene-graph traces, whose residual at rest stays below a tenth of a metre per second.

param_proposals.name: p.yield_sign_slowed_max_speed
param_proposals.convention: Yield-sign approach convention: the speed at or below which a vehicle at a yield-controlled entrance counts as having slowed, so that it can give way at the entrance without a mandatory halt; taken as the crawl speed design practice assigns to a yield-controlled approach.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book and MUTCD practice for yield-controlled approaches, where a 10 mph approach speed is the design basis for giving way without stopping.

param_proposals.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Stop-point convention of the approach reading: the bound within which an act counts as at the place the words name -- the stop line, the crosswalk or the view point -- covering the width of the marking and the position error of the body outline.
param_proposals.source: Marking-geometry and localisation practice: a transverse line about half a metre wide plus the position error of a body outline.

param_proposals.name: p.intersecting_way_view_distance
param_proposals.convention: Intersection sight-distance convention: the length of the intersecting way that must be visible in each direction from the stopping point for approaching traffic to be seen before the crossing is begun.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book intersection sight-distance tables for a crossing manoeuvre at urban approach speeds.

param_proposals.name: p.yield_headway_time
param_proposals.convention: Gap-acceptance convention: the headway, at the approaching vehicle's own speed, within which that vehicle is read as so close to the junction as to constitute an immediate hazard, being the time a crossing vehicle needs to clear its path.
param_proposals.source: Critical gap and follow-up headway practice for crossing manoeuvres (Highway Capacity Manual).

param_proposals.name: p.yield_conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: Conflict-avoidance convention: the time ahead of the observation over which a closest approach under constant velocities is read as the 'danger of a crash' the right-of-way definition names, rather than as a passing of two road users on diverging paths.
param_proposals.source: Surrogate-safety practice for time-to-conflict measures at junctions (post-encroachment and time-to-collision thresholds of two to three seconds).

param_proposals.name: p.yield_min_clearance
param_proposals.convention: Conflict-avoidance convention: the clearance between the nearest points of two bodies below which a closest approach is read as a failure to grant precedence rather than as a safe passing.
param_proposals.source: Lateral and longitudinal clearance practice for passing a road user at low speed in a junction.

segmentation.text: Except when traffic is being controlled by a police officer or a traffic-control signal:
When proper signs have been erected,
the driver of a vehicle

shall stop or yield at a clearly marked stop line or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is none, then at the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.

After having stopped or, in the event of a yield sign, slowed or stopped, the driver shall yield the right-of-way to other vehicles which have entered the intersection from such through highway or which are approaching so closely on such through highway as to constitute an immediate hazard during the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection.

elements.justification: 'traffic' is the term DEF-NRS-484A-285 defines, 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel', admitted as the aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and claimed as one atom. 'being controlled by a police officer' is dev.human_direction, 'a person directing traffic and the direction given; role is police_officer, flagger, school_crossing_guard, railroad_flagger; indication is stop, proceed, slow, turn(dir)', read with role police_officer, which is DEF-NRS-484A-180's 'officer authorized to direct or regulate traffic'; the atom carries the direction given, so a person present but directing nothing does not engage the exception. 'or a traffic-control signal' is dev.traffic_signal, 'a signal head', the device by which traffic is 'alternately directed to stop or proceed' as DEF-NRS-484A-290 requires. The controlling is dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection', read on the junction the subject approaches or on its own approach carrier, which rel.occupies, st.travel_region, st.lane_enters and st.intersection bind to the subject's own approach, so that a signal governing another junction of the scene does not excuse the duty. dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position, and no halt place is read from it.

'proper signs' are, in this section, the stop sign and the yield sign its own words name: dev.stop_sign is the 'regulatory sign requiring a full halt' and dev.yield_sign the 'regulatory sign requiring yielding without a mandatory halt'. 'have been erected' is read as the sign's presence on the road governing the subject's approach: dev.governs gives 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', read on the carrier the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region) whose entrance end is the junction (st.lane_enters, st.intersection), so the sign read is the one governing this approach and not any sign of the scene. Which of the two signs governs decides which act the obligation owes.

'the driver of a vehicle' binds the subject: DEF-NRS-484A-080 makes the driver the one who drives or is in actual physical control of the vehicle, and the ontology reads 'the driver' through the vehicle's controlled motion, so the duty binds that vehicle, of the admitted aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom. The mapping index maps the same words to the same atom.

'shall stop' is the halt DEF-NRS-484A-255 defines, 'complete cessation from movement', carried by drv.motion.standstill within the speed tolerance its contract names; 'or yield', owed where the governing sign is a yield sign (dev.yield_sign, 'regulatory sign requiring yielding without a mandatory halt', dev.stop_sign being the sign that requires the halt, dev.governs tying each to this approach), is carried by kin.speed, 'magnitude of velocity', at or below p.yield_sign_slowed_max_speed at the place. The place is read in the words' own order: st.stop_line, 'the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device', then st.crosswalk, 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection', each tied to the subject's own entrance by st.entrance_of, 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks ... the line or crossing a vehicle approaching through that carrier halts at or before', with st.lane_enters giving 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end', st.travel_region the kind the carrier quantifier ranges over and rel.occupies the anchor to the subject's own carrier; then the point at which st.sight_along_way, 'the distance along a way, in each direction from the point of that way nearest a road user, within which another vehicle on that way could be seen from the road user's eye at the observation ... the smaller of the two directions', reaches the view distance, on the way st.on_way and st.highway bind. prim.region_offset_along gives which side of the mark the subject is on along the carrier's designated direction st.lane_direction, and st.region_geometry the distance between the subject's body and the mark that the stop-point tolerance bounds; the primitive's own inputs are not claimed beside it. 'before entering the crosswalk', and the entry into the junction the act precedes, are the event drv.motion.region_entry denotes, 'comes to overlap a structure region at the observation'. 'approaching traffic' is DEF-NRS-484A-285's aggregate, claimed as the single atom ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic. st.sight_along_way is not a stand-in for whether an actual road user is seen (rel.visible): the words require a view of the way whether or not anyone is on it. st.intersection is not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line.

applicability: The subject vehicle approaches an intersection -- it occupies a carrier whose entrance end is that junction -- and a stop sign or a yield sign governs that carrier. The duty does not apply where a police officer is directing the traffic at that junction or on that carrier, or where a traffic-control signal governs it.
obligation: Before the subject enters that intersection it must have halted, or where the governing sign is a yield sign halted or come down to a speed at or below p.yield_sign_slowed_max_speed, at the place the words name in their order. The event is the subject's entry into that intersection; the target is the approach carrier it occupies whose entrance end is that junction. The place is the stop line recorded as marking that carrier; where the carrier's stop lines are observed and none marks it, the crosswalk recorded as marking that carrier; where neither is marked, the point on that carrier nearest the junction at which the sight along the crossing way, in the lesser of its two directions, is at least p.intersecting_way_view_distance. The act counts at the place where the subject's speed is at or below p.standstill_speed_tolerance, or under a yield sign at or below p.yield_sign_slowed_max_speed, while the distance between its body and the mark is at most p.stop_point_tolerance and it has not yet passed the mark, the side read by the sign of prim.region_offset_along along the carrier's designated direction; an act whose footprint already overlaps the junction is not at the place. The search runs back from the entry observation and ends at the start of that approach -- the last observation before the entry at which the subject, on a carrier the mark marks, was off the mark, short of it and farther from it than p.stop_point_tolerance -- or at the subject's previous entry into the same junction, and at nothing else: not at another junction, not at the first observation of the recording, not at a distance travelled. Where the search finds the act the duty is met; where it reaches either end without it the duty is violated; where it reaches neither end, because the history begins before the recording or because the carrier's association with the mark or its direction is unobserved, the duty is unknown. Where a mark's entrances are observed and exclude the subject's carrier, the place is read from the next words in order and the duty is not unknown on that ground.

narrowings.why: 'or yield' at a yield sign is read as the subject's speed at the place being at or below p.yield_sign_slowed_max_speed -- the sign's own contract requires 'yielding without a mandatory halt' -- together with the precedence the next sentence states, which the second node of this line carries. A reading that demanded a halt under a yield sign would hold the subject to more than the words.

'a clearly marked stop line' is read as the stop line the scene represents: the line's presence is the evidence of its clear marking, and the paint's clarity or wear is not modelled. The reading relaxes neither which place governs nor the act and its timing.

'the through highway' is read as the crossing highway at whose entrance the subject's governing stop or yield sign stands: DEF-NRS-484A-275 makes a through highway one at whose entrances traffic is required by law to yield in obedience to such a sign, and the sign governing this approach is the observable evidence of that designation.

'has a view of approaching traffic' is read as the sight along the crossing way reaching at least p.intersecting_way_view_distance in the lesser of its two directions, not as the driver's actual perception, which no trace carries.

'proper signs have been erected' is read as the presence on the road of a stop sign or a yield sign governing the subject's approach carrier: the feature's presence is the observable evidence of its proper erection by an authority.
'the driver of a vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: who or what is at the controls is not observable, and the duty binds that vehicle's conduct.

The point the third place names has no region in a scene: it is written as an observation at which the subject, on the approach carrier and not yet in the junction, has the sight along the crossing way at or above p.intersecting_way_view_distance. 'Nearest the intersection' is not read as a spatial minimum, and the start of the approach for that place is the last observation on the carrier at which that sight fell short of the distance.

'the through highway' is read as a highway region the junction lies on that the subject's own approach carrier does not lie on. dev.governs records the carrier a sign governs and no atom places a sign at a way's entrance, so the crossing way is identified by the junction and the carrier, not by the sign's position on it.

The search back from the entry counts the act at its onset — the rising edges of the act since the start of the search's latest run — so an act that already held at the first observation after the end of the search is not counted.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A side road meets a highway. A stop sign governs the car's approach lane, a stop line is recorded as marking that lane, and no officer or signal controls the junction. The car rolls over the line at 4 m/s and enters the junction, its speed never falling to the standstill tolerance anywhere on the approach from the line's upstream zone onward. No other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same junction and stop sign. The car comes to rest with its speed at zero while its body is within the stop-point tolerance of the stop line and short of it, then enters the junction. The scene holds no other road user and the verdict is still decided.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The same geometry, but a police officer stands in the junction giving a proceed indication to the traffic on the car's approach. The exception holds, so the rule is not engaged.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The car enters the junction without halting and a stop sign stands beside its approach, but the source does not report which travel regions that sign governs, so whether a proper sign has been erected for this approach is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A yield sign, not a stop sign, governs the car's approach, with a stop line marking the lane. The car does not halt but comes down to 3 m/s within the stop-point tolerance of the line before entering the junction: under a yield sign the words require no mandatory halt.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A stop sign governs the approach, and the lane's stop lines and crosswalks are observed with none marking it. The car crosses the point nearest the junction at which the sight along the crossing way reaches the view distance at 6 m/s and enters without ever halting: the third place governs and no halt is found.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: The recording begins with the car already between the stop line and the junction, inside the line's stopping zone, and the car then enters the junction. No halt is recorded, and the recording holds neither the start of the approach upstream of the line nor a previous entry of the car into that junction.
scenarios.boundary: the stretch of the approach upstream of the stop line's stopping zone, at which the car entered that zone, lies before the first observation of the recording

param_proposals.name: p.standstill_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Standstill convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed reading is read as the complete cessation from movement DEF-NRS-484A-255 requires, set at the noise floor of a speed channel at rest.
param_proposals.source: Instrumentation practice for speed channels in scene-graph traces, whose residual at rest stays below a tenth of a metre per second.

param_proposals.name: p.yield_sign_slowed_max_speed
param_proposals.convention: Yield-sign approach convention: the speed at or below which a vehicle at a yield-controlled entrance counts as having slowed, so that it can give way at the entrance without a mandatory halt; taken as the crawl speed design practice assigns to a yield-controlled approach.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book and MUTCD practice for yield-controlled approaches, where a 10 mph approach speed is the design basis for giving way without stopping.

param_proposals.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Stop-point convention of the approach reading: the bound within which an act counts as at the place the words name -- the stop line, the crosswalk or the view point -- covering the width of the marking and the position error of the body outline.
param_proposals.source: Marking-geometry and localisation practice: a transverse line about half a metre wide plus the position error of a body outline.

param_proposals.name: p.intersecting_way_view_distance
param_proposals.convention: Intersection sight-distance convention: the length of the intersecting way that must be visible in each direction from the stopping point for approaching traffic to be seen before the crossing is begun.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book intersection sight-distance tables for a crossing manoeuvre at urban approach speeds.

segmentation.text: It is unlawful for any person to drive or operate a vehicle of any kind or character at:
In any event,
a rate of speed greater than 80 miles per hour.

elements.justification: The same words as in NRS_484B_600_1a and NRS_484B_600_1c and read the same way: 'a vehicle of any kind or character' is the defined term the table resolves to DEF-NRS-484A-320, admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, carried by ru.aggregate, whose 'literal argument is an aggregate id'; 'to drive or operate' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, drv.motion.standstill read negated. Exclusions: ru.aggregate is not a stand-in for a class atom or a relational role; drv.motion.standstill is not a stand-in for the engine being off or a brake being applied.

kin.speed is the 'magnitude of velocity' in m/s, which is the 'rate of speed' the words bound; the bound is the figure the text itself states, declared as a literal in miles per hour on this span, and the comparison is that magnitude against it. Exclusion: kin.speed is the magnitude of velocity and not the acceleration along heading, which is not read; no posted sign and no judgement standard enters, the figure being the statute's own.

residues.why: The words add no observable condition and no restriction to the duty: they say that the cap binds whatever the other paragraphs of the subsection allow, so the duty is the same whether or not these words hold, and nothing in the scene is read for them.

applicability: The subject vehicle v is in motion at the observation (drv.motion.standstill false for v, with p.standstill_speed_tolerance), which is how 'to drive or operate' is read: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever is at the controls, in any event and wherever the vehicle runs.
obligation: v's speed (kin.speed) does not exceed the figure the text states, 80 miles per hour, carried as a literal in that unit.

narrowings.why: 'for any person to drive or operate' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, as the ontology's section on what is not an atom directs: a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven, and the duty binds that vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject runs along an open highway at a speed above the figure the text states.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The subject runs along the same highway at a speed below the figure the text states, holding it for the whole recording. No other road user is present in the scene.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject stands in a parking bay with its engine running, the magnitude of its velocity within the standstill tolerance, so it is not driven or operated.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject is on the highway and the source supplies no magnitude of velocity for it, so neither whether it is in motion nor whether its speed exceeds the stated figure can be told.

param_proposals.name: p.standstill_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Standstill convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed reading is read as the definition's complete cessation from movement, the bound within which measurement error and sampling cannot be told from no movement at all.
param_proposals.source: the speed resolution of vehicle-dynamics and scene-graph sources, of the order of a tenth of a metre per second.

segmentation.text: A signal of intention to turn right or left, or otherwise turn a vehicle from a direct course, shall be given continuously during not less than the last 100 feet traveled
in a business or residential district and not less than the last 300 feet traveled in any other area
prior to changing the course of a vehicle.
This rule shall be observed, regardless of the weather.

elements.justification: sig.turn_indicator is 'the turn indicator state in {off, left, right}: neither indicator lit, or the left or the right one' and sig.hand_signal is 'a driver's or rider's arm signal; meaning in {no_signal, left, right, stop_or_slow, re_enter}'; together they carry 'a signal of intention to turn right or left', the ontology directing that a signal 'of intention' is the signal itself and not a declared intention. kin.path_length, 'distance travelled along the body's path since the start of the trace, monotone', is what the window 'the last 100 feet traveled' measures: a distance-travelled window reads it as a time window reads the clock. kin.yaw_rate, 'rate of change of heading, positive when the heading turns to the left', gives the hand of the course change, so that the signal required is the indication of that hand. ru.aggregate carries 'a vehicle' by the admitted id DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. Exclusions: sig.turn_indicator is 'not a stand-in for the turn or lane change itself', which s3 carries by its concept; sig.hand_signal is not the rider's posture; kin.yaw_rate is 'not a stand-in for road curvature', no road geometry being read; kin.path_length is the subject's own travelled distance and not a position.

drv.motion.turning is 'the road user's heading is changing at the observation: the magnitude of its heading change over the window behind the observation is at least the heading change tolerance ... a state the road user is in at each observation of a bending path, in either hand', which is 'changing the course of a vehicle', the law's own 'turn right or left, or otherwise turn ... from a direct course'. 'prior to' is read from the observation at which that change is first recognized, the rise of the concept, and the window of travelled path runs back from it. Exclusions: the concept is not a stand-in for a completed turn, a steering input, the curvature of the road, a lane change, or a signal or an intention, the signal being carried on s1 by its own atoms.

assumptions.meaning: the map or trace declares that the stretch of highway the road user occupies at the observation lies within a business district or a residential district

residues.why: The words add no observable condition and no restriction: the signal is owed over the same window, in the same terms, whether or not rain, snow, wet road, ice or any other weather is present, so the duty is the same whether or not these words hold. The rule reads no weather atom for them, and nothing of the obligation is dropped.

applicability: The subject vehicle v changes its course: at the judged observation drv.motion.turning rises for v, its heading change over p.turn_recognition_window first reaching p.heading_change_noise_floor. The trace's declaration asm.in_business_or_residential_district selects the window; where the trace declares it neither true nor false the verdict is unknown.
obligation: Over the window of path travelled behind that observation -- 100 feet where asm.in_business_or_residential_district holds and 300 feet where it does not, the length selected by a condition on that declaration and measured as a distance-travelled window on kin.path_length -- v gave the signal of the hand of the course change at every observation of the window: sig.turn_indicator in the state of that hand, or sig.hand_signal with that hand's meaning. The hand is read at the judged observation from the sign of kin.yaw_rate, left positive. A window that reaches past the start of the trace leaves the verdict unknown.

narrowings.why: 'A signal of intention to turn right or left, or otherwise turn a vehicle from a direct course' is read as an indication of the hand of the course change -- the indicator lit on that hand, or an arm signal whose meaning is that hand -- and the hand is read from the sign of the road user's rate of change of heading at the observation at which the course change is recognized. A signal given on the other hand does not satisfy the duty.

'given continuously during not less than the last 100 feet traveled' and the alternative length of s2 are read as one distance-travelled window behind the observation at which the course change is recognized, the length selected by the district declaration, with the signal required at every observation of that window; the figures are the text's own.

The hand of the course change is read from the sign of kin.yaw_rate at the judged observation: strictly positive is left, strictly negative is right. At an observation whose rate of change of heading is exactly zero no hand is read, so the duty of s1 is stated for a course change whose rate of change of heading is non-zero where it is recognized; the signal is required on the hand the sign gives and a signal on the other hand does not satisfy it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The trace declares the stretch the subject occupies to lie in a business district. The subject runs straight, then bends to the right until its heading change over the recognition window reaches the noise floor; over the whole hundred feet of path travelled before that observation its indicator was off and no arm signal was given.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The trace declares the stretch to lie in no business or residential district. The subject lights its left indicator early and holds it lit over more than three hundred feet of travelled path before its heading change to the left reaches the noise floor. No other road user is present in the scene.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject runs along its lane for the whole recording, its heading change over the recognition window never reaching the noise floor, so no course change is recognized and no signal is owed.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The trace declares a residential district and the subject's course change to the left is recognized well after the start of the recording, but the source observes neither the indicator state nor an arm signal, so whether the signal was given over the window cannot be told.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Outside any business or residential district by the trace's declaration, the subject holds its right indicator lit over the whole three hundred feet of travelled path and then bends to the left, its heading change to the left reaching the noise floor: the signal given is of the other hand.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: In a declared business district, the subject gives no indicator but the driver holds out an arm whose signal means left at every observation of the hundred feet of travelled path before its heading change to the left is recognized.

param_proposals.name: p.turn_recognition_window
param_proposals.convention: Manoeuvre-recognition convention: the window behind an observation over which a yaw rate is integrated to tell a bending path from a straight one, long enough to carry a junction turn and short enough not to merge two successive manoeuvres.
param_proposals.source: manoeuvre-recognition practice for junction turns and lane changes at urban speeds.

param_proposals.name: p.heading_change_noise_floor
param_proposals.convention: Resolution convention: the heading change over the recognition window below which an integrated yaw reading is indistinguishable from a straight course at the source's resolution; it names the resolution only and sets no measure of how sharp a course change must be.
param_proposals.source: integrated yaw-rate noise over a window of a few seconds in vehicle-dynamics and scene-graph sources.

segmentation.text: Except when traffic is being controlled by a police officer or a traffic-control signal:
The driver of a vehicle
shall stop in obedience to a stop sign or yield in compliance with a yield sign, in compliance with the manner prescribed in subsection 1 [NRS-484B-257-1], prior to entering an intersection
if a stop sign or a yield sign is erected at one or more entrances thereto
although not a part of a through highway
and shall proceed cautiously,
yielding to vehicles not so obligated to stop or yield and which are within the intersection
or approaching so closely as to constitute an immediate hazard
during the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection.

elements.justification: The same words as in subsection 1 take the same atoms. 'traffic' is DEF-NRS-484A-285's aggregate, claimed as the single atom ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic. 'being controlled by a police officer' is dev.human_direction, 'a person directing traffic and the direction given', with role police_officer, DEF-NRS-484A-180's 'officer authorized to direct or regulate traffic'; 'or a traffic-control signal' is dev.traffic_signal, 'a signal head', the device by which traffic is alternately directed to stop or proceed. The controlling is dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection', read on the junction the subject is at or on its own approach carrier, which rel.occupies, st.travel_region, st.lane_enters and st.intersection bind.

'The driver of a vehicle' binds the subject, and 'such driver' later in the sentence is the same one: the ontology reads 'the driver' through the vehicle's controlled motion, so the duty binds that vehicle, of the admitted aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom. The mapping index maps the same words to the same atom.

'a stop sign or a yield sign is erected at one or more entrances thereto' is the presence of dev.stop_sign ('regulatory sign requiring a full halt') or dev.yield_sign ('regulatory sign requiring yielding without a mandatory halt') governing at least one entrance of that junction: dev.governs gives 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', st.lane_enters 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end' -- so an entrance of the junction is such a carrier -- st.travel_region the kind those carrier quantifiers range over, st.intersection the junction, and rel.occupies the anchor tying the subject to the carrier it approaches through. No stop line or crossing is read here: the entrance is the carrier itself, not a mark upon it.

'vehicles' are road users of the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines, the admitted aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom and quantified over inside the obligation. 'not so obligated to stop or yield' is read on the road: such a vehicle reached the junction through a carrier that no stop sign and no yield sign governs, which dev.stop_sign, dev.yield_sign and dev.governs ('the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') decide on the carrier st.lane_enters gives ('the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'), st.travel_region being the kind that quantifier ranges over and rel.occupies the anchor to that vehicle's own footprint; a carrier never takes the governance of a carrier it overlaps, so the sign read is the one recorded for its own carrier. 'which are within the intersection' is rel.occupies on the junction region of kind st.intersection. 'yielding' is DEF-NRS-484A-210's right 'to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another vehicle ... unless one grants precedence to the other': the subject grants precedence by not coming into contact with such a vehicle (rel.contact, 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap') and by not letting its closest approach to it fall below the clearance, which prim.closest_approach_within and prim.closest_approach_distance give under constant velocities within the horizon and rel.surface_gap measures between the nearest points of the bodies, with kin.speed the subject's own speed.

'during the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection' fixes when the duty is read: rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') on the junction region of kind st.intersection gives the subject's being across or within it, and kin.speed, 'magnitude of velocity', above p.standstill_speed_tolerance gives its moving. st.intersection is not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line: the words name the junction itself.

operationalizations.convention: A low-speed stopping-distance convention bounds the caution: crossing the junction after obeying the sign, the subject's speed stays at or below p.cautious_proceed_max_speed, the speed at which a vehicle can be brought to rest within the junction's conflict area on seeing a road user it must give way to. The degree of the hazard enters through the conflict-avoidance convention, the closest approach under constant velocities within p.yield_conflict_horizon staying clear of p.yield_min_clearance, so that the bound moves with the proximity and closing speed of the road users the same sentence names rather than switching on their presence alone.

operationalizations.standard: or approaching so closely as to constitute an immediate hazard
operationalizations.convention: Gap-acceptance convention for a crossing from a sign-controlled entrance. 'So closely' is the other vehicle's distance to the junction, which st.region_geometry gives as 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it', read on a vehicle on a carrier entering that junction (rel.occupies, st.travel_region, st.lane_enters): the vehicle is so close where that distance is at most its own speed (kin.speed) times p.yield_headway_time, so the bound moves with its speed -- a faster approach makes a greater distance count, a slower one a smaller. The immediacy is read in the same breath by the conflict-avoidance convention: the closest approach between the two bodies under constant velocities within p.yield_conflict_horizon falling below p.yield_min_clearance, measured between the nearest points of the bodies by rel.surface_gap. Both figures are the reading's, from gap-acceptance tables for a crossing manoeuvre.

residues.why: 'although not a part of a through highway' adds no observable condition: it is concessive, saying that the cautious proceeding and the yielding are owed even where the junction is not part of a through highway, so the duty is the same whether or not it is. Reading it as a condition would make the rule apply only at junctions off a through highway, which is narrower than the words.

applicability: A stop sign or a yield sign is erected at one or more entrances of the intersection the subject is at, whether or not the junction is part of a through highway; the subject's footprint overlaps that junction and its speed is above p.standstill_speed_tolerance, so that it is moving across or within it. The duty does not apply where a police officer is directing the traffic there or a traffic-control signal governs the junction or the approach.
obligation: At every observation at which the subject is moving across or within that intersection it must proceed cautiously -- its speed at or below p.cautious_proceed_max_speed -- and must grant precedence to every vehicle of the aggregate whose approach carrier into that junction is governed by no stop sign and no yield sign and which either lies within the junction or approaches so closely as to constitute an immediate hazard: its distance to the junction at most its speed times p.yield_headway_time, or its closest approach to the subject under constant velocities within p.yield_conflict_horizon below p.yield_min_clearance. Granting precedence is: no contact with that vehicle, and no closest approach to it within p.yield_conflict_horizon below p.yield_min_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'not so obligated to stop or yield' is read as a vehicle whose own approach carrier into that junction is governed by no stop sign and no yield sign: the obligation the words refer to is the one this subsection and subsection 1 place on a sign-controlled approach, and the sign governing the carrier is the observable fact that decides it. The rule is not read as composing another rule's verdict, since a rule counts as complied with where it is not engaged, which would say nothing about whether that vehicle was obligated.

'yielding' is read as granting precedence in the two observable ways open to a vehicle already moving across or within the junction: no contact with the privileged vehicle, and no closest approach within the horizon closer than the clearance.
'is erected' is read as the sign's presence on the road at an entrance of the junction: the feature's presence is the observable evidence of its erection by an authority.
'The driver of a vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: who or what is at the controls is not observable, and the duty binds that vehicle's conduct.

The clearance the duty keeps is read with both measures the span's justification names, because no primitive gives the closest approach between the nearest points of two bodies: where the two draw together within p.yield_conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within), the duty is breached when the centre distance at that closest approach (prim.closest_approach_distance) is below p.yield_min_clearance, and also when the present distance between the nearest points of the bodies (rel.surface_gap) is below it, which catches two long bodies passing closer than the clearance while their centres stay further apart. Where the two do not draw together at all, neither figure is read: a road user moving away is granted precedence.

The duty is read at every intersection the applicability's selection picks: the obligation quantifies universally over regions of kind st.intersection and rewrites that whole selection (the subject's footprint overlapping the junction, its moving, and a stop or yield sign at one of the junction's entrances) as the guard of the implication, since a region bound in the applicability is not in scope in the obligation.

The approach carrier through which a protected vehicle reached the junction is read as a travel region other than the junction itself: a junction is no approach to itself, and st.lane_enters is not recorded on it, so reading the junction as its own entrance would leave the vehicle's obligation unknown wherever it stands in the junction.

The two figures of the hazard convention are read as alternatives: a vehicle approaches so closely as to constitute an immediate hazard where its ground distance to the junction is at most its own speed times p.yield_headway_time, or where the closest approach of the two centres within p.yield_conflict_horizon falls below p.yield_min_clearance. The record states both in one breath without saying which governs where, and either alone is enough to make the approach an immediate one. The nearest-point figure is not read a second time here: it measures the clearance of the duty itself (ob1), so that the set of vehicles the duty protects is decided by the approach and not by the breach.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A stop sign governs the car's entrance to a junction where the crossing street's entrances carry no sign. The car halts, then pulls across the junction at 9 m/s while a van whose entrance carries no sign is within the junction, and the two bodies touch.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same junction and stop sign. The car crosses the junction at 3 m/s and no other road user is in the scene at any observation: nothing is owed precedence, and the verdict is decided with the subject alone.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The car crosses a junction at which no stop sign and no yield sign is erected at any entrance: the condition fails and the rule is not engaged.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The car crosses the junction while a van is within it, but the source does not report which travel regions the signs of the junction govern, so whether the van's approach was obligated to stop or yield is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The car crosses the junction at 3 m/s while a van whose own entrance also carries a stop sign is within the junction: the van is itself obligated to stop, so it is not among the road users this duty protects, and no unobligated vehicle is near.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The car crosses the junction at 3 m/s, below the cautious bound, while a van on the unsigned crossing street is twenty metres from the junction at 20 m/s -- within its speed times the headway bound -- and their closest approach under constant velocities within the horizon falls to a metre.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: No other road user is near, but the car crosses the junction at 12 m/s after halting at its stop sign: the cautious-proceeding bound is exceeded on its own.

param_proposals.name: p.standstill_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Standstill convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed reading is read as the complete cessation from movement DEF-NRS-484A-255 requires, set at the noise floor of a speed channel at rest.
param_proposals.source: Instrumentation practice for speed channels in scene-graph traces, whose residual at rest stays below a tenth of a metre per second.

param_proposals.name: p.cautious_proceed_max_speed
param_proposals.convention: Low-speed stopping-distance convention: the speed at or below which a vehicle crossing a junction from a sign-controlled entrance can be brought to rest within the junction's conflict area on seeing a road user it must give way to, taken as the 10 mph figure design practice uses for such an entry.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book stopping-sight-distance table at low design speeds, and MUTCD practice treating a sign-controlled entry as a crawl speed.

param_proposals.name: p.yield_headway_time
param_proposals.convention: Gap-acceptance convention: the headway, at the approaching vehicle's own speed, within which that vehicle is read as so close to the junction as to constitute an immediate hazard, being the time a crossing vehicle needs to clear its path.
param_proposals.source: Critical gap and follow-up headway practice for crossing manoeuvres (Highway Capacity Manual).

param_proposals.name: p.yield_conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: Conflict-avoidance convention: the time ahead of the observation over which a closest approach under constant velocities is read as the 'danger of a crash' the right-of-way definition names, rather than as a passing of two road users on diverging paths.
param_proposals.source: Surrogate-safety practice for time-to-conflict measures at junctions (post-encroachment and time-to-collision thresholds of two to three seconds).

param_proposals.name: p.yield_min_clearance
param_proposals.convention: Conflict-avoidance convention: the clearance between the nearest points of two bodies below which a closest approach is read as a failure to grant precedence rather than as a safe passing.
param_proposals.source: Lateral and longitudinal clearance practice for passing a road user at low speed in a junction.

segmentation.text: When a vehicle enters an intersection controlled by a traffic-control signal which is installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered, but is inoperative at the time the vehicle enters the intersection,

the driver of the vehicle shall proceed as if a stop sign had been erected at each entrance to the intersection and shall stop at a clearly marked stop line or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is none, at the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.
After making such a stop,
the driver
shall proceed cautiously,
yielding to vehicles which have previously completed a stop or are within the intersection.

elements.justification: The same words as in the first node of this line take the same atoms. 'a vehicle' is DEF-NRS-484A-320, admitted as ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle and claimed as one atom. 'enters an intersection' is drv.motion.region_entry ('comes to overlap a structure region at the observation') on a region of kind st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges'), anchored by rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') so that the junction read is the subject's own. 'a traffic-control signal ... installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered' is dev.traffic_signal, 'a signal head' with the 'uncovered attribute for an installed head whose faces are not covered', the only device atom by which traffic is 'alternately directed to stop or proceed' as DEF-NRS-484A-290 requires; 'controlled by' is dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection, read as control of the junction itself'; 'is inoperative at the time the vehicle enters the intersection' is dev.inoperative, 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication', read at the entry observation. dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position, and the place of the halt is read in c1 from its own marks.

'such a stop' refers to the halt the previous sentence requires, and the condition carries that halt with every qualification the referring words keep: the same subject, the same place and the same order before the entry. The halt itself is drv.motion.standstill, which carries DEF-NRS-484A-255's 'complete cessation from movement' within the speed tolerance its contract names. The place is carried as the previous sentence states it: st.stop_line ('the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device') or st.crosswalk ('marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection'), each tied to the subject's own approach by st.entrance_of ('the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks ... the line or crossing a vehicle approaching through that carrier halts at or before') and st.lane_enters ('the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'), with st.travel_region the kind that carrier quantifier ranges over and rel.occupies the anchor to the subject's own footprint; else the point at which st.sight_along_way ('the distance along a way, in each direction from the point of that way nearest a road user, within which another vehicle on that way could be seen') reaches the view distance, on the way st.on_way and st.highway bind. prim.region_offset_along gives the side along the carrier's designated direction st.lane_direction, and st.region_geometry the distance between the subject's body and the mark that the stop-point tolerance bounds. A weaker fact -- a halt anywhere, or a halt at another junction -- would not be the stop the words refer to, so the full qualification is carried here and the defining words are marked sibling only because the duty they state belongs to the other node.

'the driver' is the driver of the same vehicle the trigger reads; DEF-NRS-484A-080 makes the driver the person who drives or is in actual physical control of the vehicle, and the ontology reads 'the driver' through the vehicle's controlled motion, so the duty binds that vehicle, whose class is the admitted aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom.

'vehicles' is DEF-NRS-484A-320, the admitted aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom for the road users quantified over inside the obligation. 'which have previously completed a stop' is drv.motion.standstill read at an earlier observation ('complete cessation from movement' within the speed tolerance), on a carrier whose entrance end is the same junction: st.lane_enters gives that entrance relation, st.travel_region the kind its carrier quantifier ranges over, rel.occupies the anchor to that other road user's own footprint. 'or are within the intersection' is rel.occupies on a region of kind st.intersection, the relation whose contract is exactly a footprint overlapping the junction region. 'yielding' is DEF-NRS-484A-210's right of one vehicle 'to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another ... unless one grants precedence to the other': the subject grants precedence by not entering the junction while such a road user is within it -- drv.motion.region_entry is the entry event -- and by not closing on it, which rel.surface_gap ('distance between the nearest points of two bodies ... zero when they touch or overlap'), prim.closest_approach_within and prim.closest_approach_distance measure under constant velocities within the horizon, with kin.speed the subject's own speed and rel.contact ('the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap') the outcome the precedence is there to prevent. rel.surface_gap is not a stand-in for an order of arrival, which the words carry themselves through the earlier halt and the present occupancy; rel.contact is not a stand-in for a near miss, which is why the closest-approach primitives are claimed beside it.

operationalizations.convention: A low-speed stopping-distance convention bounds the caution: moving off from a required halt, the subject's speed where it enters and crosses the junction is held at or below p.cautious_proceed_max_speed, the speed at which a vehicle can halt within the junction's conflict area on seeing a road user it must give way to; the degree of the hazard enters through the conflict-avoidance convention, the closest approach under constant velocities within p.yield_conflict_horizon staying clear of p.yield_min_clearance, so that the bound moves with the proximity and the closing speed of the road users the same sentence names rather than switching on their presence alone.

applicability: The subject vehicle enters an intersection governed by a traffic-control signal that is installed, uncovered and inoperative at that entry, and at an earlier observation on the same approach the subject came to a complete halt at the place the first sentence names -- the stop line marking its approach carrier, else the crosswalk marking it, else the point at which the sight along the crossing way reaches p.intersecting_way_view_distance. The halt is searched for back from the entry to the start of that approach or to the subject's previous entry into the same junction, as the first node of this line states it; where that history begins before the recording the condition, and so the rule, is unknown.
obligation: From that entry on, while the subject is moving across or within the intersection, it must proceed cautiously -- its speed at or below p.cautious_proceed_max_speed -- and must grant precedence to every road user of the vehicle aggregate that either completed a halt earlier on a carrier whose entrance end is the same junction or lies within the junction at the observation: the subject must not enter the junction at an observation at which such a road user lies within it, must not come into contact with it, and must not let its closest approach to it under constant velocities within p.yield_conflict_horizon fall below p.yield_min_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'yielding' is read as granting precedence in the three observable ways the right-of-way definition's 'danger of a crash unless one grants precedence' admits on a trace: no entry into the junction while such a road user is within it, no contact, and no closest approach within the horizon closer than the clearance. A driver's deference that shows in none of these is outside what a trace can check.

'have previously completed a stop' is read as a halt at an earlier observation of the recording by that road user on a carrier whose entrance end is the same junction: the words give no place for the other road user's halt, and the junction's own entrances are the places at which such a halt is owed.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: who or what is at the controls is not observable, and the duty binds that vehicle's conduct.

'which have previously completed a stop' is read as a standstill of that road user, on a carrier whose entrance end is this junction, at some observation of the recording up to and including the judged one: the language looks back to an observation at or before the one it judges, and a road user standing at an entrance at the judged observation has come to the halt the words describe.

the clearance of p.yield_min_clearance is read on two measurements the record names together: the centre distance at the closest approach under constant velocities within p.yield_conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_distance), and the clearance between the nearest points of the two bodies at the observation (rel.surface_gap); precedence is denied where either falls below it while the centres approach within the horizon.

the duty is read at every observation from the qualified entry at which the subject's footprint still overlaps the junction region, that unbroken occupancy carrying 'from that entry on, while the subject is moving across or within the intersection'; it is not read after the subject's footprint has left the junction.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car halts at the stop line of its lane at a junction whose signal heads are installed, uncovered and dark, then accelerates into the junction at 8 m/s while a van that halted a moment earlier at the opposite entrance is already within the junction region: the subject enters while the van lies inside, and its speed is above the cautious bound.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same junction and inoperative signal. The car halts at its stop line and then crosses the junction at 3 m/s. No other road user is in the scene at all, so nothing is owed precedence and the verdict is still decided.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The same junction, the same dark heads, but the car never halts anywhere on its approach before entering the junction: the condition that it made such a stop does not hold, so this rule is not engaged and only the first node of the line judges the conduct.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The car halts at its stop line and moves off into the junction, but the source does not report whether the other road user's footprint overlaps the junction region, so whether a road user was within the intersection when the subject entered is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The same junction and inoperative signal. The car halts at its stop line, a van that halted earlier at the opposite entrance is within the junction, and the car stays at rest until the van has left the junction region, then crosses at 3 m/s with a closest approach well clear of the clearance bound.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The car halts at its stop line, then crosses the junction at 3 m/s, below the cautious bound, but passes within half a metre of a van already within the junction, the closest approach under constant velocities falling below the clearance bound within the horizon: precedence is not granted even though the speed is low.

param_proposals.name: p.standstill_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Standstill convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed reading is read as the complete cessation from movement DEF-NRS-484A-255 requires, set at the noise floor of a speed channel at rest.
param_proposals.source: Instrumentation practice for speed channels in scene-graph traces, whose residual at rest stays below a tenth of a metre per second.

param_proposals.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Stop-point convention of the approach reading: the bound within which a halt counts as at the place the words name -- the stop line, the crosswalk or the view point -- covering the width of the marking and the position error of the body outline.
param_proposals.source: Marking-geometry and localisation practice: a transverse line about half a metre wide plus the position error of a body outline.

param_proposals.name: p.intersecting_way_view_distance
param_proposals.convention: Intersection sight-distance convention: the length of the intersecting way that must be visible in each direction from the stopping point for approaching traffic to be seen before the crossing is begun.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book intersection sight-distance tables for a crossing manoeuvre at urban approach speeds.

param_proposals.name: p.cautious_proceed_max_speed
param_proposals.convention: Low-speed stopping-distance convention: the speed at or below which a vehicle moving off from a required halt into a junction can be brought to rest within the junction's conflict area on seeing a road user it must give way to, taken as the 10 mph figure design practice uses for a stop-controlled entry.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book stopping-sight-distance table at low design speeds, and the MUTCD practice of treating a stop-controlled entry as a crawl speed.

param_proposals.name: p.yield_conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: Conflict-avoidance convention: the time ahead of the observation over which a closest approach under constant velocities is read as the 'danger of a crash' the right-of-way definition names, rather than as a passing of two road users on diverging paths.
param_proposals.source: Surrogate-safety practice for time-to-conflict measures at junctions (post-encroachment and time-to-collision thresholds of two to three seconds).

param_proposals.name: p.yield_min_clearance
param_proposals.convention: Conflict-avoidance convention: the clearance between the nearest points of two bodies below which a closest approach is read as a failure to grant precedence rather than as a safe passing.
param_proposals.source: Lateral and longitudinal clearance practice for passing a road user at low speed in a junction.

segmentation.text: If the driver of a vehicle
intends to turn
at an intersection and:
Both intersecting highways are two-directional:
After entering the intersection,
the left turn
must be made so as to leave the intersection to the right of the centerline of the highway being entered.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is a legal aggregate and the definitions table admits DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle for this law; ru.aggregate carries 'membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id', so the words are claimed as the one atom with that id. The mapping index maps these same words in NRS_484B_400_2a to this atom and they mean the same here. Exclusions: not a stand-in for a named road-user class, since no class atom is used and the aggregate stays one atom; not a stand-in for a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle, so 'the driver' is not carried by the aggregate but read through the vehicle's controlled motion (narrowing on this span).

Reuse of the mapping index for these same words in NRS_484B_400_2a. st.intersection is 'the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges', the junction the words name; rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region', anchors the vehicle to the carrier it is on, and st.lane_enters gives 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end', so the intersection the words single out is the one the carrier the vehicle occupies enters; st.travel_region, 'the union of the kinds a device can govern: a lane and the kinds that refine it ... a roadway ... or an intersection', is the kind the carrier quantifier ranges over. Exclusions: st.intersection is not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line, neither of which is read; st.lane_enters is not a stand-in for lane connectivity or for the subject's presence in the intersection, which rel.occupies carries; st.travel_region is not a stand-in for the extent of a highway, read by its own atom on s4.

Reuse of the mapping index for these same words in NRS_484B_400_2a. DEF-NRS-484B-073 defines a two-directional highway as 'an undivided highway upon which vehicles are allowed to proceed in opposite directions': st.median_or_divider, 'physical barrier or dividing section between roadways', carries 'undivided' by the absence of such a region on the way, and st.lane_direction, 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in ... a roadway, one-way roadway or shoulder', carries 'proceed in opposite directions' by two carriers of the same way carrying opposed designated directions. The two ways are reached through the junction: st.lane_enters names the carriers whose entrance end is that intersection, st.travel_region is the kind they are quantified by, st.roadway 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic' is the kind whose directions are designated, st.on_way 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on' and st.highway 'the entire public way between its boundary lines' give the highway each carrier lies on, st.intersection the junction itself, and rel.occupies anchors the subject. Exclusions: st.median_or_divider is read for the physical barrier its contract denotes and not for a legal designation of a highway, which would be an assumption; st.lane_direction is local to its carrier, which is why it is read on the carriers of each intersecting way and not at a point; st.roadway is not a stand-in for the sidewalk, which is not read.

drv.motion.region_entry is 'the road user's footprint comes to overlap a structure region at the observation: it overlaps the region at the observation and did not overlap it at the observation before ... the event of that coming to overlap', which is 'entering the intersection'; the region formal is bound to the intersection s3 singles out, so the entry is into that junction and not into any region of its kind. rel.occupies anchors the vehicle on the region and st.intersection is the kind the region quantifier names. The mapping index maps 'prior to entering an intersection' to the same carriers. Exclusions: the concept is not a stand-in for lying within the region afterwards, which rel.occupies carries on its own, nor for the carrier the road user came through.

drv.motion.left_turn is 'the road user has turned to the left: counting from the onset of the turning ... the heading change accumulated since that onset reaches at least the turn angle ... to the left', which is 'the left turn' the words name, the manoeuvre whose manner the obligation governs. Exclusions: the concept is not a stand-in for a signal or a declared intention (the intention of s2 is carried by int.turn), not for a steering input, not for the curvature of the road, not for a lane change, and not for a reversal of the direction of travel, which is a larger angle with its own concept.

'leave the intersection' is drv.motion.region_exit, 'the road user's footprint ceases to overlap a structure region at the observation: it does not overlap the region at the observation and did overlap it at the observation before ... the event of that ceasing to overlap', with its region formal bound to the intersection s3 singles out, so the departure is from that junction; rel.occupies anchors the vehicle and st.intersection is the kind that region quantifier names. 'the centerline of the highway being entered' is a st.centre_line region, 'the marking, or the geometric centre, dividing the two directions of a two-way roadway', tied to the way by st.on_way, 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on', on the st.highway region, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines', that the vehicle occupies at that observation (rel.occupies). 'to the right of' is prim.region_lateral_offset, 'the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user ... the component, perpendicular to the road user's heading, of the vector from its reference point to the point of the region's boundary nearest that reference point': the centre line lies to the vehicle's left, so the vehicle lies to its right. Exclusions: prim.region_lateral_offset 'does not establish that the road user is on the carrier', which rel.occupies does; st.centre_line is the dividing marking or geometric centre and no lane or lane adjacency stands in for it; st.highway is not a stand-in for the roadway, and the words name the highway being entered.

intentions.meaning: the source's current plan for the road user is that it turn, to either hand, at the region named as the declaration's target

applicability: The subject vehicle v occupies a carrier whose entrance end is an intersection i (st.lane_enters, the carrier quantified over st.travel_region, rel.occupies); the source's current declaration for v at i is int.turn; both highways that meet at i are two-directional, each way carrying no median or dividing section (st.median_or_divider absent on it) and carriers of its roadway carrying opposed designated directions (st.lane_direction), the ways reached by st.on_way and st.highway from the carriers that enter i; v has entered i (drv.motion.region_entry on i at the judged observation or at an earlier one); and v has made a left turn (drv.motion.left_turn, with p.turn_onset_yaw_rate, p.left_turn_angle and the step bound p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph).
obligation: At the observation at which v leaves i (drv.motion.region_exit on the intersection i the applicability binds), v lies to the right of the centre line of the highway it then occupies: for the st.highway region h with rel.occupies(v, h) at that observation there is a st.centre_line region c with st.on_way(c, h) whose signed lateral offset from v, prim.region_lateral_offset (left positive), is at least p.lateral_offset_resolution. Where no such centre line is observed on that way the obligation is unknown, not met.

narrowings.why: 'the driver of a vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the ontology's section on what is not an atom directs that 'drives', 'operates' and 'the driver' are read through the vehicle's controlled motion, a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven, and the duty binds that vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.

'the highway being entered' is read as the st.highway region the vehicle occupies at the observation at which it leaves the intersection, and 'the centerline' of it as a centre-line region lying on that way (st.on_way). The words leave open which way is meant; this is the way the vehicle is on once it is clear of the junction, the junction itself lying on every way that meets there.

'to the right of the centerline' is read as the centre line's signed lateral offset from the vehicle standing at or above p.lateral_offset_resolution on the left-positive side, the magnitude below which the side a region lies on is not distinguishable at the source's resolution; the side is read across the vehicle's own heading, which at the departure from the junction lies along the way entered.

The junction whose departure the duty judges is the one the applicability selects, and that selection is restated in the obligation as having held at the judged observation or at an earlier one: the carrier whose entrance end is the junction, the subject's presence on it, and the declaration of a turn at that junction. A carrier is an approach to the junction, so the subject is no longer on it at the observation at which its footprint leaves the junction, which is the observation this duty judges.

'the highway being entered' is read for every highway region the subject occupies at the departure, not for one of them: where the subject's footprint lies on more than one way at that observation, the centre line of each must lie to its left, so no way is picked in the subject's favour.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Two undivided ways, each with carriers of opposed designated directions, cross; the trace declares the subject's intention to turn at that junction; the subject enters the junction and its accumulated heading change to the left passes the turn angle, so a left turn is made. At the observation at which its footprint ceases to overlap the junction it is on the far side of the entered way's centre line, the centre line lying to its right.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same two two-directional ways, the same declared intention, the same entry and left turn; at the observation at which the subject's footprint ceases to overlap the junction the centre line of the way it then occupies lies to its left by more than the lateral-offset resolution. No other road user is present in the scene.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject runs straight through the same junction: the trace declares no intention to turn for it at that junction and its accumulated heading change never reaches the turn angle, so no left turn is made.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Every other condition holds -- two two-directional ways, the declared intention, the entry, and a departure from the junction on the left of the entered way's centre line -- but the source supplies no rate of change of heading for the subject, so whether it has turned to the left cannot be told.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The way being entered carries a median dividing its two directions, so the intersecting ways are not both two-directional; the subject, with a declared intention to turn, enters the junction, turns left and leaves it on the left of that way's centre line.

param_proposals.name: p.lateral_offset_resolution
param_proposals.convention: Lateral-offset convention: the magnitude of a signed lateral offset below which the side a region lies on is not distinguishable at the source's resolution, so that an offset smaller than it decides no side; it names the source's resolution only and sets no measure of how far from the line a vehicle must be.
param_proposals.source: the lateral accuracy of mapped region boundaries and of a body's reference point in a scene-graph source, of the order of half a metre.

param_proposals.name: p.left_turn_angle
param_proposals.convention: Turn-recognition convention: the heading change accumulated since the onset at which a turn to the left is recognized as made, taken as the angle at which a body has committed to a left turn at a junction rather than a lane change or a drift within its lane.
param_proposals.source: manoeuvre-recognition practice for junction turns, which treats an accumulated heading change of about a quarter turn as a committed turn.

param_proposals.name: p.turn_onset_yaw_rate
param_proposals.convention: Manoeuvre-onset convention: the rate of change of heading above which a body is read as turning rather than running straight, set at the noise floor of a yaw reading so that the onset of a manoeuvre is told from lane-keeping corrections.
param_proposals.source: yaw-rate noise of vehicle-dynamics and scene-graph sources at open-road speeds.

segmentation.text: A vehicle
shall not be turned so as to proceed in the opposite direction
upon any curve,
or upon the approach to or near the crest of a grade,
where such vehicle cannot be seen by the driver of any other vehicle approaching from either direction within 500 feet.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is a legal aggregate and the definitions table admits DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle for this law; ru.aggregate carries 'membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id'. Exclusions: not a stand-in for a named road-user class, no class atom being used; not a stand-in for a relational role, the words naming the vehicle itself and not its driver.

drv.motion.u_turn is 'the road user's direction of travel upon a way has reversed ... the magnitude of the heading change accumulated since that onset reaches at least the reversal angle ... while the road user's footprint overlaps a way', and its contract carries the very words of this obligation: 'the turning of a vehicle upon a highway so as to proceed in the opposite direction', 'whether accomplished by one continuous movement or not', so halts and rearward movements between the onset and the reversal do not end the manoeuvre. Exclusions: it is not a stand-in for a turn through a smaller angle, which has its own concept, nor for travel against a designated direction of travel, nor for a reversing movement, nor for a signal or a declared intention.

st.curvature is 'horizontal curvature of the roadway at a point, as a magnitude (1/m, never negative): a bend to either hand has the same value', which is 'any curve'; the words name the feature and no size of it, so it is carried by the magnitude standing clear of zero, at or above p.curvature_resolution, a parameter that names the source's resolution only and no measure of how sharp a bend must be. rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region', anchors the vehicle on the region whose curvature is read, and st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic', is the kind that region quantifier names, the curvature being the roadway's. Exclusions: st.curvature is not the crest of a grade, read on s4 by its own atom, and not the sight distance the bend restricts, read on s5; st.roadway is not a stand-in for the sidewalk, which is not read.

st.crest is 'the place on a roadway's longitudinal profile where the slope changes from rising to falling in the direction of travel, carried as a region with a reference point and a boundary, so the ground distance from a road user to it is read through st.region_geometry', which is 'the crest of a grade'; 'the approach to or near' it is that ground distance, st.region_geometry giving 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it', at most p.crest_approach_distance. rel.occupies anchors the vehicle on the roadway and st.roadway is the kind the region quantifier names for the way the profile belongs to. Exclusions: st.crest is expressly 'not a stand-in for the slope at a point (st.grade)', which is why no grade atom is read, nor for 'the view a crest restricts (st.sight_distance)', read on s5 by its own atom, nor for 'a horizontal bend (st.curvature)', read on s3; st.region_geometry is not a stand-in for occupancy, which rel.occupies carries. The ground distance carries the words as they read: 'the approach to or near' the crest reaches the vicinity on either hand of it, which is what a distance from the body to the crest region states, the atom carrying the crest as a region and the distance to it.

st.sight_distance is 'the distance along the road within which a vehicle at a point and another vehicle on the road could see each other, from the eye of either driver to the body of the other vehicle at the height convention the source declares: both the view of approaching traffic from that point and its being seen by drivers approaching it, whether or not any road user is there'. The words 'such vehicle cannot be seen by the driver of any other vehicle approaching from either direction within 500 feet' are exactly that quantity at the vehicle's place falling short of the stated 500 feet, and the contract's 'whether or not any road user is there' is why the duty binds the subject with no other vehicle in the scene. rel.occupies anchors the vehicle on the road whose sight distance is read and st.roadway is the kind that region quantifier names. Exclusions: it is 'not a stand-in for whether an actual road user saw, or could see, another at an observation (rel.visible)', and the words ask of any approaching driver, not of one present; not for 'the clarity of the air (env.visibility)'; and not st.sight_along_way, whose contract is the view from a road user's own eye along a way, while the words ask whether the vehicle can be seen at its place.
