The contract's one value for the place carries 'from either direction' as the words read it, the quantity being defined over both directions of the road at once, and it carries 'cannot be seen by the driver of any other vehicle' as the place's own sight distance, which the contract states 'whether or not any road user is there', so no perception of an actual driver is read.

applicability: The subject vehicle v occupies a roadway, and at one and the same moment while the reversal is under way (the words join the place and the sight condition by 'where'): either the horizontal curvature of the roadway at v's place stands at or above p.curvature_resolution, or the ground distance from v's body to a st.crest region on the roadway is at most p.crest_approach_distance; and the sight distance of v's place (st.sight_distance) falls short of 500 feet.
obligation: v does not turn upon the way so as to proceed in the opposite direction: the rule is violated where drv.motion.u_turn is recognized for v (with p.turn_onset_yaw_rate, p.u_turn_reversal_angle and the step bound p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph) and the applicability's conditions held together at a moment of that act; it is complied with where the conditions so held and no such act is recognized.

onset.words: counting from the onset of the manoeuvre -- the observation at which the magnitude of its rate of change of heading first rose above the onset yaw rate
onset.justification: The concept's contract fixes the act's observed beginning at that observation, and the only quantity it reads there is kin.yaw_rate, 'rate of change of heading, positive when the heading turns to the left (counter-clockwise)'. Exclusion: kin.yaw_rate is 'not a stand-in for road curvature', which this node reads on s3 by its own atom for the place, not for the manoeuvre.

occasion.recognition: the observation at which the magnitude of the heading change accumulated since that onset first reaches the reversal angle, which is where the concept rises; the later observations at which the accumulated change still holds that angle are not the act again.

under_way.words: the magnitude of the road user's rate of change of heading has stood above the onset yaw rate since the onset and the accumulated heading change has not yet reached the reversal angle
under_way.justification: An observation inside the act is told from one before it began by the road user's own motion: its rate of change of heading, the quantity the concept's onset and accumulation read. No place or region tells them apart, since the vehicle occupies the same bend, the same crest vicinity and the same place before the manoeuvre begins.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject runs along a bend whose horizontal curvature stands well above the resolution, and the sight distance of its place falls short of the figure the text states. On that bend it swings through more than the reversal angle and proceeds back the way it came.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same bend with the same short sight distance; the subject turns off into a side way, its accumulated heading change staying far below the reversal angle, and never proceeds in the opposite direction. No other road user is present in the scene.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: On a straight and level stretch, no crest region within the approach distance and the place's sight distance well beyond the stated figure, the subject swings through more than the reversal angle and proceeds back the way it came.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject reverses its direction on a bend whose curvature is recorded, but the source declares no sight distance for the places along it, so whether the vehicle could be seen within the stated distance cannot be told.

scenarios.name: occasion_s3
scenarios.narrative: The subject begins the reversal on the bend and completes it where the alignment has run out straight: the curvature stands above the resolution at the onset and the first part of the manoeuvre only, and the sight distance at those same observations falls short of the stated figure.

scenarios.name: occasion_s3_outside
scenarios.narrative: The subject runs along the bend, leaves it, and only then, on a straight stretch with no crest region within the approach distance, swings through more than the reversal angle; the curvature stands above the resolution only at observations before the onset, while the sight distance is short throughout.

scenarios.name: occasion_s4
scenarios.narrative: The subject begins the reversal with the crest region within the approach distance of its body and completes it farther down the grade, beyond that distance; the alignment is straight throughout and the sight distance at the observations near the crest falls short of the stated figure.

scenarios.name: occasion_s4_outside
scenarios.narrative: The subject passes the crest, runs on until the crest region lies beyond the approach distance, and only then swings through more than the reversal angle on a straight stretch; the crest was within the approach distance only at observations before the onset, while the sight distance is short throughout.

scenarios.name: occasion_s5
scenarios.narrative: The subject reverses its direction on a bend whose curvature stands above the resolution at every observation of the manoeuvre, and the sight distance of its place falls short of the stated figure at the onset and the first part of the manoeuvre, rising above it before the reversal is complete.

scenarios.name: occasion_s5_outside
scenarios.narrative: The subject runs on the bend through a stretch whose sight distance falls short of the stated figure, and begins and completes the reversal farther along the same bend, where the sight distance at its place exceeds the stated figure at every observation from the onset onwards.

param_proposals.name: p.turn_onset_yaw_rate
param_proposals.convention: Manoeuvre-onset convention: the rate of change of heading above which a body is read as turning rather than running straight, set at the noise floor of a yaw reading so that the onset of a manoeuvre is told from lane-keeping corrections.
param_proposals.source: yaw-rate noise of vehicle-dynamics and scene-graph sources at open-road speeds.

param_proposals.name: p.u_turn_reversal_angle
param_proposals.convention: Reversal convention: the accumulated heading change at which the definition's proceeding in the opposite direction is recognized, set below a half turn so that a reversal completed in stages, or one leaving a residual angle to the way, still counts as made.
param_proposals.source: manoeuvre-recognition practice for U-turns, which admits a reversal short of a full half turn.

param_proposals.name: p.curvature_resolution
param_proposals.convention: Map-geometry resolution convention: the magnitude of horizontal curvature below which a surveyed road alignment is indistinguishable from a tangent at the resolution of the source, a radius of the order of a kilometre. It names the source's resolution only and sets no bound on how sharp a bend must be for the duty to bind.
param_proposals.source: highway alignment survey practice, in which curves of radius above about a kilometre are recorded as tangents in the road geometry of a map or simulator.

param_proposals.name: p.crest_approach_distance
param_proposals.convention: Crest sight-distance convention: the distance from a crest within which the crest's vertical curve restricts the view of the road beyond it, taken as the length of the crest vertical curve of the design standard at open-road design speed; it bounds 'the approach to or near' the crest on either side.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book crest vertical curve lengths and stopping sight distance tables for open-road design speeds.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle within an intersection intending to turn to the left shall yield the right-of-way to any vehicle approaching from the opposite direction which is within the intersection or so close thereto as to constitute an immediate hazard,
but such driver, having so yielded
and having given a signal when and as required,
may make such left turn
and the drivers of all other vehicles approaching the intersection from the opposite direction
shall yield the right-of-way to the vehicle making the left turn.

elements.justification: 'having given a signal' is the signal the left-turning vehicle emits: sig.turn_indicator, whose 'state is off, left or right: neither indicator lit, or the left or the right one', shown as left, or sig.hand_signal, 'a driver's or rider's arm signal; meaning is no_signal, left, right, stop_or_slow, re_enter', given as left. sig.turn_indicator is 'not a stand-in for the turn or lane change itself', and it is not used for one here: the turn is carried separately by its own concept in c3, and this span carries only the indication. 'when and as required' is read through the signalling convention: a left indication at some observation in the window p.turn_signal_advance_window behind the turn's recognition. The condition is read on the left-turning vehicle the obligation quantifies over, not on the subject.

'may make such left turn' names the manoeuvre drv.motion.left_turn denotes, 'the road user has turned to the left: counting from the onset of the turning ... the heading change accumulated since that onset reaches at least the turn angle ... to the left', read on the left-turning vehicle while its footprint overlaps the junction: rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') on a region of kind st.intersection ties the turn to the junction the subject approaches, so that a left turn made elsewhere in the scene does not raise this duty. The concept states the turning of the body only, and neither a signal nor a declared intention stands in for it.

'the drivers of all other vehicles' binds the subject: the driver is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, so the subject is each other vehicle of the admitted aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom. 'approaching the intersection' is the ontology's own reading, 'a carrier it occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is that intersection (st.lane_enters)', with st.travel_region the kind that carrier quantifier ranges over and st.intersection the junction at which the left turn is made. 'from the opposite direction' is read, as the ontology directs for these words, through that carrier's designated direction st.lane_direction being opposed to the direction of the carrier by which the left-turning vehicle reached the junction, their normalised dot product at or below the negative of p.same_direction_cosine_tolerance; rel.oncoming is expressly not a stand-in for the direction a road user approaches from, and the left-turning vehicle's heading swings through its turn, so the carriers and not the headings are read.

'the vehicle making the left turn' refers to the road user c3 already binds -- the vehicle of the admitted aggregate ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed here as one atom, whose left turn in that junction c3's element carries with its concept -- so the obligation reads that same road user and re-claims no manoeuvre of its own: the turning is the condition that raises the duty, and the duty itself is conduct of the subject towards it. Its presence in the junction is rel.occupies on a region of kind st.intersection. 'shall yield the right-of-way' is DEF-NRS-484A-210's right 'to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another vehicle ... unless one grants precedence to the other': the subject grants precedence by not coming into contact with that vehicle (rel.contact) and by not letting its closest approach to it fall below the clearance, which prim.closest_approach_within and prim.closest_approach_distance give under constant velocities within the horizon and rel.surface_gap measures between the nearest points of the bodies, with kin.speed the subject's own speed. rel.contact is not a stand-in for a near miss, which is why the primitives stand beside it.

applicability: There is a vehicle t of the aggregate within an intersection making a left turn there, which has complied with the duty of NRS_484B_253_o1 ('having so yielded') and has given a left indication, by indicator or by arm signal, at some observation in the window p.turn_signal_advance_window behind the recognition of its turn; and the subject vehicle occupies a carrier whose entrance end is that intersection and whose designated direction is opposed to the direction of t's approach carrier.
obligation: At every such observation the subject must grant precedence to t: it must not come into contact with t, and must not let its closest approach to t under constant velocities within p.yield_conflict_horizon fall below p.yield_min_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'shall yield the right-of-way' is read as granting precedence in the two observable ways open here: no contact with the turning vehicle, and no closest approach within the horizon closer than the clearance.
'the drivers of all other vehicles' is read through each vehicle's controlled motion: who or what is at the controls is not observable, and the duty binds that vehicle's conduct.

Granting precedence is read as a duty on the subject's own proceeding: where the subject's speed is zero it grants precedence by standing, and the clearance bounds are read on a subject that is itself moving. Contact is forbidden whether or not the subject moves.

The clearance the span's atoms measure is bounded in both of the ways they give, each at p.yield_min_clearance: the gap between the nearest points of the two bodies at the observation (rel.surface_gap), and, where the centres approach within p.yield_conflict_horizon, the centre distance at that closest approach (prim.closest_approach_distance), which is undefined where they do not approach and then bounds nothing.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A van within a junction has yielded to the opposing stream, shows its left indicator through the two seconds before its turn is recognized, and turns left. The subject car occupies the opposing approach lane entering the same junction and drives on into the van's path, the two bodies touching.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same junction and the same signalled, yielded left turn by the van. The subject car brakes on its approach and stays more than ten metres clear of the van throughout, no closest approach within the horizon coming near the clearance bound.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car occupies the opposing approach lane of a junction in which no vehicle is making a left turn at all: no road user raises the duty, so the rule is not engaged.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A van makes a signalled left turn in the junction the subject approaches, but the source does not report whether the van's footprint overlaps the junction region, so whether the turn is the one made in that intersection is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The van turns left in the junction and has yielded to the opposing stream, but its indicator stays off and it gives no arm signal in the window behind the recognition of the turn: the weaker fact -- a turn made without the signal the words require -- leaves the other drivers' duty unraised, and the rule is not engaged.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The van signals left and turns, but it did not comply with its own duty to yield under the first node of this section: it turned across an oncoming vehicle that was within the junction. Having not so yielded, it raises no duty on the other drivers.

param_proposals.name: p.same_direction_cosine_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Heading-agreement convention: the cosine of the largest angle between two directions still read as the same direction, set at thirty degrees; its negative is the bound at which two directions are read as opposed.
param_proposals.source: The thirty-degree sector convention used for same-direction and opposed-direction tests in traffic conflict analysis.

param_proposals.name: p.turn_signal_advance_window
param_proposals.convention: Signalling convention: the window behind the movement within which an indication counts as the signal given for it, taken from the advance-notice practice for a turn.
param_proposals.source: Driver-signalling practice and the advance-notice intervals of state vehicle codes.

param_proposals.name: p.turn_onset_yaw_rate
param_proposals.convention: Manoeuvre-onset convention: the rate of change of heading above which a body is read as turning rather than running straight, set above the yaw noise of a vehicle holding its lane.
param_proposals.source: Yaw-rate channel noise and lane-keeping figures from instrumented-vehicle studies.

param_proposals.name: p.left_turn_angle
param_proposals.convention: Turn-recognition convention: the heading change accumulated since the onset at which a turn to the left is recognized as made, rather than as a lane change or a bend taken.
param_proposals.source: Manoeuvre-recognition practice: half the ninety-degree heading change of a right-angle junction turn.

param_proposals.name: p.yield_conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: Conflict-avoidance convention: the time ahead of the observation over which a closest approach under constant velocities is read as the 'danger of a crash' the right-of-way definition names, rather than as a passing of two road users on diverging paths.
param_proposals.source: Surrogate-safety practice for time-to-conflict measures at junctions (post-encroachment and time-to-collision thresholds of two to three seconds).

param_proposals.name: p.yield_min_clearance
param_proposals.convention: Conflict-avoidance convention: the clearance between the nearest points of two bodies below which a closest approach is read as a failure to grant precedence rather than as a safe passing.
param_proposals.source: Lateral and longitudinal clearance practice for passing a road user at low speed in a junction.
